projects.title: Ritz-Carlton Naples
projects.summary: Restoring the infrastructure behind a landmark hotel. NorthStar assembled a temporary distribution system with more than 7 MW of emergency generation and over 20 miles of cable during the critical first weeks. The team then connected six chilled-water systems to restore environmental control and coordinated the remaining recovery sequence with hotel leadership and project partners.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Ian caused severe wind and storm-surge damage at the beachfront Ritz-Carlton in Naples. Flooding submerged the ground-floor power distribution, chilled-water systems, and air-handling equipment. NorthStar Recovery Services was selected to lead the recovery effort, with the hotel's essential engineering systems and the local electrical grid unavailable.

Within hours of arrival, NorthStar assessed the extent of the infrastructure loss and began coordinating a temporary power solution. Working with resource partners, the team assembled more than 7 MW of emergency generation and installed over 20 miles of distribution cable during the critical first weeks.

Once temporary power was established, NorthStar connected six chilled-water systems to restore environmental control. This allowed recovery to advance through the affected hotel floors while limiting further moisture-related damage.

NorthStar coordinated the work sequence with hotel leadership and other project stakeholders. The team met the stated key milestones on time and within budgetary constraints, supporting the return of key hotel operations. This emergency recovery scope was separate from the property's broader renovation and expansion program.

projects.title: ProLogis / FedEx Facility
projects.summary: A damaged logistics campus prepared for rebuilding in 100 days. NorthStar mobilized demolition and remediation teams, worked two twelve-hour shifts, and coordinated daily structural reviews with Sigma Engineering Solutions. Crews dismantled, cataloged, crated, and relocated 12 sortation units, then rebuilt them at another ProLogis facility. The demolition scope included concrete processing and reinstatement to site specifications.
projects.overview:
On March 3, 2020, an EF-3 tornado tore through Mt. Juliet, Tennessee and struck the ProLogis industrial complex housing critical FedEx operations. Two buildings (650,000 sqft and 500,000 sqft) sustained structural damage across roof systems, interior burn lines, and concrete infrastructure. Inbound and outbound logistics were disrupted.

NorthStar Recovery Services mobilized within hours. Our teams established command, secured the site, and set the scope for total demolition and remediation of both buildings, including crushed concrete placed back per site specifications. Working shoulder to shoulder with Sigma Engineering Solutions to continuously validate structural integrity, NRS operated around the clock on two twelve-hour shifts. The project was completed in 100 days with no injuries and no environmental impacts, even as the COVID-19 pandemic reached its first peak mid-project.

The work stabilized damaged industrial assets and returned the site ready for rebuilding.

The buildings' compromised structures required continuous engineering oversight. Sigma Engineering conducted daily structural surveys, verified roof and ponding conditions via aerial drone, and issued clearances before each shift. NorthStar installed protective barricades early in the project, and those barricades performed as designed. No further structural degradation occurred during the 100 days of demolition.

In parallel with demolition, NorthStar dismantled 12 FedEx sortation units, the automated sortation infrastructure that moves inbound packages through the facility. Our crews cataloged, crated, and relocated each unit, then rebuilt them at a separate ProLogis facility. That turnkey approach let FedEx resume logistics operations without waiting for the primary buildings to be restored.

COVID-19 protocols were implemented on-site as the pandemic escalated. Enhanced PPE, crew spacing, and daily health screening kept the project moving without a single health-related stoppage. Over the course of 100 days and more than 50,000 shift hours, NRS completed every scope element on schedule, handed the site back with full concrete reinstatement, and maintained a zero-incident safety record.

NorthStar brought self-performing demolition, remediation, and reconstruction support under a single accountable field leadership team. The field team coordinated the demolition, remediation, and equipment-relocation scopes throughout the response.

projects.title: Capital One Tower
projects.summary: A coordinated high-rise response through two hurricanes. NorthStar removed damaged glazing and interior materials, extracted water, and installed more than 3 MW of temporary power. The drying operation combined over 55,000 CFM of desiccant capacity, truck-mounted extraction, and equipment distributed through the tower. An on-site housing camp supported crews when regional accommodation was scarce.
projects.overview:
Hurricanes Laura and Delta successively damaged Capital One Tower in Lake Charles during 2020. The approximately 400,000-square-foot, 22-story building sustained extensive glazing damage, roof damage, and water intrusion. The recovery took place during the COVID-19 pandemic and regional disruption following the storms.

After Laura, more than a thousand exterior glass panes required carefully planned removal. Water penetrated approximately 20 feet into the building's south side across its floors. NorthStar removed damaged glazing, extracted tens of thousands of gallons of water, removed affected materials and contents, introduced drying equipment, and addressed the compromised roof.

Approximately six weeks into the effort, Delta damaged additional glazing on the north and west sides and drove water into the building's core. The tower was left without power and extensively exposed to the weather, with 60 tenants and more than 1,000 employees displaced.

NorthStar coordinated more than 3 MW of temporary power and installed over 55,000 CFM of desiccant drying capacity. Twelve truck-mounted extraction units supported water removal. Additional dehumidifiers, more than 200 air movers, and portable desiccants served the floors. A custom debris chute extended to the 20th floor for interior demolition waste.

At peak, more than 120 personnel were on site. An on-site camp with 25 accommodation trailers, washing and sanitation facilities, meals, and water supported crews when hotel space was unavailable. Pandemic operating protocols were integrated into the response. The response recorded zero OSHA recordables and no reported positive COVID-19 cases.

projects.title: Flagler College
projects.summary: Water-loss recovery shaped around historic preservation. NorthStar responders arrived within two hours and used moisture mapping to define the work. An 8,000 CFM desiccant stabilized the environment before selective demolition and abatement. Restricted access and protected windows required a custom debris-removal arrangement using a boom lift and purpose-built chute.
projects.overview:
In July of 2022 Historic East Ponce Hall was impacted by a significant water loss. This loss was the result of a sprinkler line rupture that was discovered by Flagler staff some time after it had occurred, allowing the water a substantial amount of time to migrate through the structure. Detailed damage assessments and moisture mapping was conducted and findings indicated that the loss had affected 4 floors of the dormitory, with more than 40 individual spaces incurring significant water damage. Within two hours NorthStar first responders were on site to begin planning and mobilizing equipment and personnel.

Due to the historic nature of the property and building materials, great care was taken during each phase of the project. Environmental stabilization was the main priority for the first several hours, ensuring that the potential for additional secondary damage was properly mitigated. NorthStar achieved this with the use of one 8000CFM desiccant, which was used to dry affected materials as gently as possible. The next phase was perhaps more critical - selective demolition of affected materials while simultaneously preserving those areas with no damage at all. The project became more complex with the discovery of hazmat within the building materials, which elevated the project from a major water loss recovery to an abatement project as well.

In addition to being a large loss, the timeline requested by the client was very stringent. Tight and narrow spaces inside the building on the upper floors required NorthStar operators to think outside the box to be able to effectively remove demolition waste and abatement bags. Due to the historic nature of the structure, NorthStar was not permitted to remove windows and windows casements, so a solution was found using a combination of boom lift and construction of a custom trash chute.

After nearly 6 months of 24 hour operations on site, the project was completed on time and to the exact specifications of the client. At its peak, this project saw 125 specialized laborers on site, all working in concert to deliver the industry-leading service that NorthStar clients have come to expect.

projects.title: El Conquistador Resort
projects.summary: Sustaining resort operations through an island-wide emergency. NorthStar prepositioned responders 15 days before landfall and coordinated with resort management. The team supported guest checks, food and water, temporary power, fuel deliveries, roof repairs, and large-scale drying. Hotel employees and local laborers joined the effort, while satellite equipment restored critical communications during the recovery.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Maria damaged guest rooms, villas, roofs, and infrastructure at El Conquistador in Fajardo in September 2017. Island-wide power and communications failures complicated the response. NorthStar had responders positioned on Puerto Rico 15 days before landfall and maintained contact with resort management to plan equipment and recovery needs.

At landfall, the resort accommodated 365 guests and 255 hotel employees. NorthStar supported physical checks on guests when communications failed, helped provide food, water, and clean beds, and employed the hotel's 255 employees in initial recovery tasks. Satellite-based equipment restored critical communications approximately 15 days after the storm.

The described recovery scope covered a property with 750 rentable spaces. Work included debris removal, roof repairs, mechanical and electrical support, infrastructure recovery, water mitigation, and environmental control. NorthStar supported continued use of the resort by first responders and military personnel.

Approximately 400 local laborers participated. Equipment included 1.5 MW of portable power, 80,000 CFM of desiccant drying capacity, 255 LGR dehumidifiers, and nearly 800 air movers. NorthStar secured daily deliveries of 12,000 gallons of diesel fuel to support the operation.

The resort returned to full operating capacity after nearly 18 months and more than 37,000 hours of recovery work.

projects.title: North Central Bronx Hospital
projects.summary: Preparing critical hospital space during the COVID-19 surge. NorthStar mobilized multiple shifts to remove aged systems, interior finishes, and unused spaces while addressing hazardous materials. The preparation scope covered more than 100,000 square feet across eight floors. Intensive work over a four-week period supported the reconstruction sequence and required close coordination within an active healthcare environment.
projects.overview:
During the early 2020 COVID-19 emergency, NYC Health + Hospitals called on NorthStar to prepare existing space at North Central Bronx Hospital for intensive-care expansion.

NorthStar mobilized personnel and resources to prepare more than 100,000 square feet across eight floors. Crews removed aged systems, interior finishes, and unused spaces while addressing hazardous materials within the demolition scope. Multiple shifts over a four-week period supported the urgent reconstruction sequence.

NorthStar completed its construction efforts ahead of schedule on May 5, 2020, with zero OSHA recordables. Its work supported the hospital's broader expansion and ability to receive patients during the surge. The clinical capacity increase and patient-care outcomes were the result of the wider hospital program and are not attributed solely to NorthStar.

projects.title: Philadelphia Energy Solutions Refinery
projects.summary: Industrial decommissioning at the scale of a city district. NorthStar integrated asbestos and hydrocarbon remediation with demolition and recycling. The work included removal of tank bottoms and residual hydrocarbons, processing concrete for reuse or recycling, and recovering steel and non-ferrous metals. This combined approach addressed the facility's structures and environmental materials within the same major decommissioning scope.
projects.overview:
NorthStar was awarded the contract for the demolition and decommissioning of the Philadelphia Energy Solutions Refinery, the largest and oldest oil refinery on the East Coast. The facility was situated on a 1300 acre site in South Philadelphia along the banks of the Schuykill River. NorthStar’s scope of work included asbestos and hydrocarbon remediation, industrial demolition, and recycling of steel and non-ferrous metals.

NorthStar teams completed: - Over 1.5 million man-hours worked without an OSHA recordable safety incident. - Removal and recycling of 180,000 gross tons of steel - Removal and recycling of 12 million pounds of non-ferrous metals - Removal and processing of 80,000 cubic yards of concrete for recycling or reuse. - 9 million gallons of tank bottoms and miscellaneous hydrocarbons removed for disposal. - 40,000 cubic yards of asbestos containing materials safely removed for disposal.

projects.title: Rockport-Fulton High School
projects.summary: Students back on campus 41 days after Harvey. NorthStar arrived within three hours after the storm passed and installed temporary power and large-scale drying within twelve hours of arrival. Crews remediated water damage, removed debris and damaged structures, rebuilt campus areas, and replaced roofing and HVAC equipment. Temporary classrooms and restrooms helped maintain education alongside the construction work.
projects.overview:
In August of 2017 Hurricane Harvey tore across the Gulf Coast of Texas where it made its first of three landfalls. Directly in its path was Rockport, Texas, home to the Rockport-Fulton High School. During the landfall of Hurricane Harvey winds in excess of 140mph and torrential rain caused extreme damage to most structures in the area, including the local high school. Once the storm had passed it was quite obvious that the high school had incurred significant damage. One gymnasium was destroyed and over 50 roof-mounted air handlers were torn from their anchors and tossed to the ground below leaving gaping holes in the roof where water was free to pass to the interior of the building causing widespread water damage. Exterior features such as light poles, fences, athletic field scoreboards, and trees were completely destroyed.

Upon closer inspection it was discovered that roughly 90% of the roof required repair and/or replacement.

NorthStar was on-site within 3 hours of the storms passing to begin damage assessments and the formulation of the Initial Scope of Work. Recovery activities included water damage remediation throughout the entire campus, demolition of the most damaged structures, significant debris cleanup, reconstruction of campus buildings, re-installation of over 50 new HVAC units, and replacement of nearly the entire roof.

Within 12 hours of NorthStar’s arrival on-site temporary power and large-scale desiccant dehumidification was installed to begin drying out the affected building materials and mitigating further secondary damage. NorthStar was also engaged to install temporary classrooms and restrooms so that students could return to school despite parts of the main facility being unusable. One of the most significant challenges throughout this project was maintaining normal operation while working alongside students and faculty who were also present in the school.

Over 200 workers logged more than 68,000 hours spread across two 12-hour daily shifts for two months. Just 41 days after Hurricane Harvey made landfall, Rockport-Fulton High School was reopened. NorthStar’s quick response and efficient management of such a large-scale project allowed the academic curriculum to be salvaged despite students missing nearly two months of class time.

projects.title: AIG Campus Recovery
projects.summary: Four priority buildings remediated in under four months. NorthStar began assessments as soon as access was safe, pumped floodwater from the buildings, and sequenced demolition, debris removal, and drying. More than 10 MW of portable power supported critical systems, while over 100,000 CFM of desiccant drying capacity served the campus. At peak, more than 800 laborers worked under dedicated supervision and project management.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Harvey brought prolonged heavy rainfall and severe flooding to the Houston area in August 2017. Torrential downpours caused waterways in Houston to overflow and flood the surrounding areas. AIG’s Houston Campus received several feet of flood water in all but one of its high-rise buildings. Basements and first floor levels of each building were inundated with over 10’ feet of flood water causing damage to both structure and contents contained therein.

NorthStar First Responders arrived on-site as soon as it was safe to do so and began damage assessments. Large water pumps were provided to pump out the flood water from the buildings in an initial effort to secure the properties. Once the water had been removed, demolition, debris removal, and dry-out began. NorthStar placed over 100,000 CFM of desiccant drying units throughout the campus and over 10 megawatts of portable power to restore critical power systems.

Crews operated around the clock in an effort to restore normal operation to the campus. At the peak of operation, there were over 800 laborers, 25 supervisors, and 3 project managers. Over 500 tons of debris was removed from four priority buildings, including destroyed contents and building materials resulting from extensive interior demolition. Full remediation of damages was completed in just under 4 months, and reconstruction was scheduled to take place shortly thereafter.

projects.summary: Cooling-tower removal with operations maintained. NorthStar verified utility isolation and protected systems remaining in service. projects.overview: The Scope of Work included the complete removal of two cooling towers in significantly deteriorated condition and in close proximity to operational equipment and service lines in an active facility. Northstar ensured that utility isolations were executed and systems to remain live demarcated and protected. The demolition was executed by dismantlement and cutting components into manageable sections for loading to waste and scrap containers, utilizing small tools and hand methods with crane support to ensure no interruption to the operational processes. NorthStar coordinated its efforts with millwrights to salvage fan motors and other components for future use. The foundations and pedestals supporting the cooling towers were protected and preserved for reuse, as well. The work was completed on schedule and with no incidents.

projects.overview:
NorthStar was contracted by Air Products to perform demolition, abatement, and full site restoration at the former Eastman Chemicals facility in Texas City, TX. The scope supported future development efforts and required strategic planning, environmental compliance, and continuous coordination within an active industrial setting.

• Structural demolition of process units, foundations, and tanks • Asbestos abatement across multiple areas and pipe racks • Pipe capping and utility isolation • Concrete removal, onsite processing, and reuse • Excavation and staging of site soils to facilitate pier removal • Reuse of stockpiled material for final backfill, compaction, and grading • Full SWPPP implementation and dewatering management • Daily coordination with the client and adaptation to evolving project needs

• 4,000 CY of concrete removed, crushed, and reused onsite • 3,100 GT of metals recycling • 51,368 CY of dirt removed, staged, and reused for backfill

NorthStar successfully felled multiple large structures using engineered methods and critical crane lifts. All demolition work was preceded by utility isolation and pipe capping. Site soils were excavated and staged to allow pier and foundation removals, then transported back into place for compaction and final grading. NorthStar managed all SWPPP compliance, dewatering, and day-to-day coordination with Air Products. The team adapted to multiple design and schedule changes while maintaining safety and project momentum.

projects.title: Aransas County Courthouse
projects.summary: Maintaining county services while clearing the path to rebuild. NorthStar established the temporary courthouse, relocated contents, and performed pre-demolition abatement. More than 75 laborers worked around the clock to protect records and meet the relocation deadline. Demolition crews then removed the damaged structure and graded the cleared site for reconstruction.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Harvey ravaged the gulf coast in 2017, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. One of the hardest hit areas was Rockport, Texas, where Aransas County is located. Many buildings were damaged and destroyed, but one important building became a priority once the dust had settled, the Aransas County Courthouse. The courthouse was so severely damaged that it was deemed too costly for repair and the county elected to embark upon a full rebuild.

To maintain continuity for the county and its legal proceedings, NorthStar was tasked with establishing a temporary courthouse. Once the temporary location was secured, NorthStar began predemolition abatement and relocation of courthouse contents.

One of the greatest challenges throughout the relocation process was maintaining the integrity of sensitive files while still completing the task within a very tight deadline. With over 75 laborers operating on a 24 hour-per-day, 7 days-per-week schedule, NorthStar emptied the damaged courthouse of all contents and began the demolition of the structure. Utilizing several pieces of heavy equipment including cranes, bulldozers, backhoes, a grader and numerous scissor lifts, the complete demolition of the damaged structure was completed on-time, safely and well within budget.

After approximately 8,500 hours worked, NorthStar successfully relocated the courthouse to its temporary location, abated and demolished the old building and graded the empty lot in preparation for reconstruction. What should have taken nearly 4 months to complete was finished by NorthStar in just over two months.

projects.title: Bank of America: Emergency Response
projects.summary: A 45-minute response within a multi-location service program. NorthStar worked under a master service agreement with Lincoln Harris and developed response procedures for these facilities. During a 2014 hot-water-line rupture, a crew and equipment arrived within 45 minutes. Moisture mapping defined the affected areas before damaged materials were removed, surfaces cleaned, and drying equipment installed.
projects.overview:
Emergency Response - Moisture Control & Dehumidification - Water Extraction - Interior & Structural Demolition - Mold Remediation - Hazardous Material Remediation.

NorthStar Recovery Services had a Master Service Agreement with Lincoln Harris for emergency response to 2,600 Bank of America locations throughout the Southeast region. NorthStar responded daily to minor leaks as well as large floods and fires affecting multi-story office buildings. NorthStar developed standard operating procedures for responding to Bank of America’s critical facilities and corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC. NRS handled emergency response for fire and water events and served as the first responder for all environmental emergencies; including spill response. As a result of the 2014 Polar Vortex, a hot water line in the 7th floor BAC restroom ruptured causing water to spray within the restroom .This affected ceiling tiles as well as drywall behind tile walls. Water migrated down through a build out chute behind restroom down to lower levels. There was also affected exposed sheetrock above ceiling. NorthStar was engaged and responded with crew and equipment within 45 minutes of loss. NRS performed a moisture map and determined extent of damage within restroom. Damaged ceiling tiles were removed and disposed. A detail clean was performed of all areas that were affected with water and dehumidification/air movement were placed to control environment and begin drying process. Weep holes were installed to expedite drying process in certain areas.

NRS handled emergency response for fire and water events and served as the first responder for all environmental emergencies; including spill response. As a result of the 2014 Polar Vortex, a hot water line in the 7th floor BAC restroom ruptured causing water to spray within the restroom .This affected ceiling tiles as well as drywall behind tile walls. Water migrated down through a build out chute behind restroom down to lower levels. There was also affected exposed sheetrock above ceiling. NorthStar was engaged and responded with crew and equipment within 45 minutes of loss. NRS performed a moisture map and determined extent of damage within restroom. Damaged ceiling tiles were removed and disposed. A detail clean was performed of all areas that were affected with water and dehumidification/air movement were placed to control environment and begin drying process. Weep holes were installed to expedite drying process in certain areas.

projects.title: Bay City School District
projects.summary: A coordinated recovery across 20 school campuses. NorthStar mobilized personnel and equipment, assessed the assigned schools, and coordinated work across the expanding portfolio. The recovery scope ultimately covered 20 of the district's 31 schools. Crews addressed water damage and building-envelope repairs while maintaining the pace required for a large education recovery program.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Michael made landfall in the Florida Panhandle on October 10, 2018, causing extensive damage in the Panama City area. The event was subsequently classified as Category 5 in National Weather Service analysis.

NorthStar mobilized personnel and resources to assist the district with school recovery. The district initially divided work among multiple recovery firms. As assignments changed during the response, NorthStar's scope expanded to 20 of the 31 district schools.

Work ranged from drying large school buildings to roof repair and rebuilding. NorthStar coordinated the growing multi-campus recovery scope and was invited to bid and interview for reconstruction work.

NorthStar completed its assigned recovery work ahead of schedule and within budget.

projects.title: Bellagio Hotel and Casino
projects.summary: A 70-hour floor cycle within an occupied resort. NorthStar organized multiple shifts to complete each released floor within a continuous 70-hour work period. Large crews and carefully allocated equipment supported the sequence, followed by scheduled pauses until the next floor became available. Visual inspection and analytical sampling were used to check the required cleanliness standards.
projects.overview:
NorthStar was retained to conduct this extremely fast-paced and detailed selective demolition where maintaining indoor air quality was a major concern. The scope of work included 2,568 rooms in a 24-story resort hotel which remained at near peak occupancy for the duration of the work without significant inconvenience to the patrons.

This demanding schedule required that each floor, comprised of 109 rooms, be completed in a straight 70-hour period. The balance of each week was a shut-down period for NorthStar, awaiting the next floor availability and its 70-hour blitz. This unusual schedule was met due to NorthStar’s ability to professionally manage multiple shifts consisting of hundreds of laborers per shift.

Direct visual inspections as well as analytical post remediation sampling confirmed that the desired degree of cleanliness was achieved. The consultant for the owner on the project was MC Consultants, and the analytical firm in charge of sampling and analysis was Forensic Analytics. All parties involved were very pleased with NorthStar’s attention to detail, control of the labor force, cleanliness and effectiveness of equipment allocation, and overall professionalism.

projects.title: Brunner Island Power Plant
projects.summary: An outage-critical demolition completed two days early. NorthStar ran two twelve-hour shifts and used a 200-foot high-reach machine to reduce the need for elevated torch-cutting and rigging. Site-specific hazard planning guided the work. Crews removed PCB-contaminated transformer oil and protected 14 existing foundations for reuse.
projects.overview:
After the successful demolition of Pennsylvania Power and Light’s ESP Unit #3 in 2006, NorthStar Recovery Services was invited back to Brunner’s Island to demolish Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) #2. To complete the task during the scheduled plant outage, NRS worked around the clock using two twelve-hour shifts each day. NRS finished two days ahead of schedule with no recorded injuries.

Safety was paramount to NRS, even with the challenge of a 24-hour-a-day schedule operating in an extremely tight work area. A Site Specific Health and Safety Plan (SSHASP), Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) and Job Safety Analysis (JSA) were created and then implemented at the field level producing a safe work environment for employees and the people working around the site.

NRS brought in the 200-foot high-reach Sennebogen for demolition at the top of the 160-foot ESP. This mitigated the need for “burning and rigging” activities at the higher levels of the unit. Without have to hoist men into the high reaches via baskets to torch the steel members in preparation for the cranes to remove them, the job was made safer with the new highreach machines.

In addition to the demolition work itself, NRS also removed and properly disposed of PCB contaminated transformer oil from the unit. Specially trained staff also addressed lead-painted components within the demolition scope. Also, 14 of the existing foundations, which were protected during the demolition operation, were re-used.

The project combined environmental-material handling and dismantlement under one coordinated field operation.

projects.title: Chase Tower: Renovation
projects.summary: Coordinated renovation across 27 occupied-tower floors. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor,'s project team coordinated system isolation and rework across electrical, mechanical, plumbing, communications, and life-safety trades. Double shifts and weekend work supported activity on as many as six floors at once. Material separation and recycling were integrated with the removal of construction and asbestos debris.
projects.overview: The 60-story Chase Tower office building, located inside Chicago’s loop, was completed in 1968 and maintained near full occupancy with both multi-floor tenants and single floor/single office tenants. LVI was contracted, under four separate contracts, to upgrade and modernize 27 floors, approximately 864,000 square feet, by removing asbestos, performing interior demolition and removing the old friable fireproofing and replace it with new fireproofing. The success of this project was predicated upon meeting an aggressive critical path schedule to alleviate tenant disruption and to facilitate construction efforts to re-occupy the floors. LVI also hired and managed subcontractors in excess of $1.6 million to perform electrical, mechanical, plumbing, communication, and life safety system isolation and rework. Additionally, LVI was required to coordinate the isolation and maintenance of the fire protection systems during construction. The majority of the work schedule necessitated working double shifts and weekends on up to 6 floors at one time. Crew size ranged from 50 to well over 100 workers, as required, for a total of 91,000 man-hours. LVI separated and recycled all metal components, wiring, and carpeting to satisfy the LEEDS requirements. All construction and asbestos debris was transported out of the building utilizing 30-yard dumpsters for a total of 2,256 loads of debris.

projects.title: Chase Tower: Water Recovery
projects.summary: Regional resources brought to a complex high-rise water loss. NorthStar's local responder arrived in under two hours. Branch equipment was reinforced by two trailers from Indianapolis within twenty hours. Crews used controlled drying, a portable desiccant, and selective demolition, coordinating union trades while maintaining three eight-hour shifts around the clock.
projects.overview:
A sprinkler supply burst on the 49th floor of Chase Tower. Heavy water damage affected floors 49 through 46, with water reaching as far as the 15th floor. The loss involved Class 3 and Class 4 water damage.

NorthStar's first responder arrived from the local branch in less than two hours. Branch equipment was followed by two trailers from Indianapolis within 20 hours. Crews performed drying and selective demolition, using a portable desiccant.

The operation ran around the clock in three eight-hour shifts, with 30 to 35 workers at its peak. Work took approximately two weeks.

Limited downtown parking, bound water across multiple floors and coordination among union trades complicated the work. The team used ASD practices and selective demolition to address those conditions.

projects.title: Climax Mine
projects.summary: Legacy-facility removal planned around mountain conditions. NorthStar provided an integrated abatement and demolition scope for Phelps Dodge. Crews removed and disposed of asbestos-containing materials, prepared structures for demolition, and packaged universal waste for disposal by the owner. Work planning accounted for the seasonal conditions and the site's operational requirements.
projects.overview:
NorthStar was contracted to do asbestos abatement and demolition of selected legacy facilities at Climax Mine near Leadville, Colorado. Climax Mine was once one of the world’s largest producers of molybdenum which was primarily used to strengthen steel in products such as armor plating and large gun barrels. The mine played an important role in steel production efforts during World War II.

NorthStar offered Phelps Dodge an integrated solution for dismantling the selected facilities by the proper removal and disposal of asbestos-containing materials in preparation for the complete structural demolition of several mine buildings, conveyors and mining equipment. NorthStar was also responsible for the removal and packaging of universal waste for disposal by the owner.

NorthStar faced many challenges in this project that included mine-site safety training for all employees, below freezing temperatures and snow conditions. NorthStar completed its portion of the project on time and returned to complete the remaining portion in the spring of 2007.

projects.title: Consolidated Edison Power Plant
projects.summary: Controlled plant dismantlement within Manhattan's infrastructure. NorthStar phased the work over five years, beginning with an office building and support structures. Later phases addressed the power-plant buildings and three roughly 300-foot stacks. Hand demolition protected exposed boundaries, while hazardous oils and PCBs were removed before the final generator dismantlement.
projects.overview:
The total dismantlement of Consolidated Edison’s steam/electricity power plant in midtown was phased over a 5-year period due to the many challenges of working in a densely constructed, compact space. The site of the plant posed the greatest problems.

The 5-block Kips Bay, multi-building campus was squeezed between the FDR Drive on the east, First Avenue on the west and the Queens-Midtown Tunnel vents on the north with the tunnel running under the property.

The first building to be demolished was the 11-story office building and support structures. The support structures, a switch house and frequency house, had to be dismantled very carefully. The roof was like that of a gymnasium. As the roof was removed there was the potential for the walls to become unstable.

The biggest challenge was the last phase. Three ±300-foot stacks towered over the two 17-story power plants. These structures had to be dismantled in a very controlled demolition until the core machinery was visible. Additionally, the walls of the power plants rose flush to the sidewalk boundary requiring hand demolition on these exposed walls to protect pedestrians, traffic and contiguous property.

The last phase, completed in August 2007, used machine power to break apart the generators after removing the PCBs and machine oil. The remaining pieces were extracted with specialized machinery.

projects.title: Covington Theological Seminary
projects.summary: Resident students returned after one week. NorthStar arrived within six hours after floodwaters receded and mobilized twelve extraction trucks. Water extraction finished in under twelve hours, followed by continuous drying and recovery work. More than fifty emergency generators supported the response, with dormitories and the cafeteria receiving priority.
projects.overview:
In March of 2016 Louisiana was hit with recordsetting amounts of rainfall that resulted in widespread flooding throughout the state. On March 10th, 2016 a college campus located in Covington, Louisiana, was overcome by flood waters from the nearby Bogue Falaya River. A total of 53 buildings throughout the campus were affected with at least one foot of standing water, including the Cafeteria, Dormitories, and Sacred Spaces.

NRS first responders arrived on-site within 6 hours of the flood waters receding and initiated the mobilization of labor and equipment. Within 4 hours 12 extraction trucks arrived on site. All water extraction was completed in less than 12 hours. Labor and additional drying equipment arrived on site shortly thereafter.

Crews operated around the clock in an effort to restore normal operation to the college campus, with focus on critical structures such as the dormitory and cafeteria. Approximately 2000 students and faculty members were displaced as a result of this event. 115 students living on campus were displaced for only one week before recovery of their living space was completed. Over 50 emergency generators were brought on-site along with a number of large-scale desiccant dehumidification systems. The project was completed in July of 2016, just 4 months after the flooding had occurred.

projects.title: Crystal River Nuclear Plant
projects.summary: A coordinated scope for nuclear-site decommissioning. NorthStar's described responsibilities encompass decommissioning, abatement, dismantlement, materials recovery, and waste disposition, with a stated site-restoration objective. The scope brings environmental handling and structural removal together under a planned sequence rather than treating each as an isolated activity.
projects.overview:
NorthStar's Crystal River scope sets out a coordinated approach to decommissioning plant systems, structures, and components, followed by dismantlement and site restoration.

Responsibilities include abatement and management of hazardous, non-hazardous, and regulated materials; removal of systems and structures; scrap recovery; and waste disposition. The stated end condition is a low-maintenance grade with established vegetation.

The program remains in decommissioning. Regulatory review and the planned site-restoration work form part of the continuing sequence toward the final end condition.

projects.title: Dayton Silo Fire
projects.summary: Specialist support brought a silo fire under control within 72 hours. NorthStar brought subject-matter experts to the site within six hours. Following an assessment of conditions, the specialists used steel injection tools to introduce nitrogen into the fire's core. The work focused on controlling the event while protecting personnel and nearby production assets.
projects.overview:
A furniture manufacturer sought NorthStar's assistance after a fire developed in a wood-debris silo at its approximately one-million-square-foot Dayton facility. The silo stood roughly 40 feet high and contained scraps from the manufacturing process.

NorthStar engaged subject-matter specialists to assess the enclosed, smoldering fire. The specialists arrived within six hours and established an approach suited to the conditions. They introduced nitrogen into the fire's core using steel injection tools, with the aim of controlling the event while protecting personnel and production assets.

The fire was extinguished within 72 hours and normal production continued. The response was managed by specialists using an approach selected for the conditions at this facility.

projects.title: Deutsche Bank Building
projects.summary: Environmental remediation planned ahead of complex deconstruction. The described scope began with smoke and fire-damage remediation, followed by cleaning and hazardous-material abatement. The planned demolition sequence called for controlled floor-by-floor removal, using compact equipment and a tower crane to manage debris in the constrained Lower Manhattan setting.
projects.overview:
In January 2008, NorthStar was engaged for remaining decontamination and deconstruction work at the former Deutsche Bank building at 130 Liberty Street. The building had been severely damaged by the collapse of the World Trade Center and later by a 2007 fire. Twenty-six stories remained when NorthStar joined the project.

The initial scope addressed smoke and fire damage. The described sequence then called for cleaning and decontamination of the remaining floors, followed by structural removal. Contamination associated with debris exposure, water intrusion, and the building materials included asbestos, lead, silica, mold, and other substances requiring controlled handling.

The structural scope covered approximately 1.1 million remaining square feet. The planned approach was floor-by-floor deconstruction using skid steers, demolition robots, compact excavators, and a tower crane to lower debris containers. The plan included processing removed concrete for use as basement ballast.

The initial plan allowed approximately nine months for cleaning and decontamination and another six months for demolition, supported by multiple shifts and a proposed workforce of 300.

The building's overall deconstruction was completed on February 28, 2011, according to the Lower Manhattan Development Corporation. This was the site-wide completion milestone.

projects.title: El Condado Hotel
projects.summary: Keeping a hotel operational while advancing storm recovery. NorthStar had personnel and equipment prepositioned on the island and began assessments within hours of the call. The team employed 145 hotel staff in early recovery, secured temporary generators and daily fuel deliveries, and deployed desiccants, dehumidifiers, and air movers. Assessments, debris cleanup, priority drying, and selective demolition advanced together.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Maria caused widespread damage and prolonged power disruption across Puerto Rico in September 2017. NorthStar supported recovery at El Condado while the property accommodated first responders and military personnel.

NorthStar personnel and equipment had been prepositioned in safe places across the island in anticipation of the storm and the ensuing recovery effort that would follow.

Once the call was made, operations personnel were on site within hours beginning preliminary damage assessments and formulating an initial scope of work to restore the 545-room hotel to pre-loss condition. In an effort to minimize lost wages, NorthStar hired all 145 of El Condado’s employees to help perform the beginning stages of recovery. This also allowed the hotel to remain open for business and continue to serve the first responders and military personnel staying there.

Within 7 days a majority of the scope of work had been completed, including damage assessments, debris cleanup, dry-out of priority areas, and selective demolition. NorthStar secured two 1MW and one 350kW generators along with a daily delivery of 12,000 gallons of diesel fuel to ensure that there was no loss of power to the hotel. To facilitate an efficient dry-out of water damaged areas, NorthStar utilized over 15,000 CFM of desiccant drying equipment, 120 LGR dehumidifiers, and nearly 400 air movers. After almost 41,000 hours worked, the hotel was back up and running at full operational capacity.

Recovery depended on maintaining equipment, materials, and fuel supplies despite substantial island-wide disruption. Due to the storms that had hit the mainland U.S. prior to Hurricane Maria, resources were stretched thin. NorthStar was able to acquire additional materials and equipment and have them shipped from the mainland in a timeframe that prevented any interruption to the recovery process and ultimately led to a successful outcome for El Condado.

projects.title: Federal Office Building #8
projects.summary: 66% of the waste stream recycled or diverted. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, worked with the government team to remove hazardous materials and demolish designated exterior and interior components. Crews gutted upper floors and service areas, used remotely operated demolition equipment in confined spaces, and separated waste streams under a LEED waste-management plan.
projects.overview:
LVI was part of a team chosen for the demolition and abatement of this former Food and Drug Administration laboratory located less than three blocks from the Capital at 200 C Street, SW, Washington, DC. LVI’s scope of work included demolition of the skin and interior spaces of floors 4, 5 and 6. Additionally, the penthouse, basement and subbasement were gutted. Because this building was once a laboratory, LVI worked with a government team to remove volatile chemicals, mercury, and other toxins. Total project covered 467,000 square feet.

The demolition program included the use of a Brokk robot. Ideal for confined spaces and selective demolition, these machines can be used remotely increasing the safety of demolition crews.

As part of a Mentor-Protégé relationship, Goel Services, the general contractor and SBA 8(a) HubZone Certified, selected Grunley construction for some of the demolition services.

LVI followed a LEED Waste Management Plan, diverting construction and demolition debris from landfill disposal, redirecting recyclable recovered resources back to the manufacturing process, and redirecting reusable materials to appropriate sites as much as feasibly possible. Over the course of the project, 3,212 tons of the waste stream, or 66% of the total waste was recycled or diverted.

This project, designated to be the new home of Homeland Security, was awarded "2006 Washington Contractor Honorable Mention Renovation Restoration" by the AGC of Metropolitan Washington DC.

projects.title: Firestone Polymers Plant
projects.period: Started August 2020; completion date not specified
projects.summary: Production resumed after a 23-day recovery. NorthStar's operations team was on site within six hours of landfall. Temporary generation supported continuous shifts involving more than 100 personnel. Work included structural repair, demolition of compromised structures, environmental remediation and a mobile office complex for Firestone staff.
projects.overview:
The Firestone Polymers Production Plant in Lake Charles, LA was severely impacted by Hurricane Laura in August 2020. A critical production facility for the conversion of raw material into rubber manufacturing products, the Lake Charles facility serves as the principal rubber supply hub for all Bridgestone and Firestone entities. The damage inflicted compromised more than 35 structures on the site as well as several key engineering support systems and processes that directly affected its ability to meet supply chain demands.

Given this deadline circumstance, NorthStar was presented with the challenge of completing repairs and recovery within a 28-day period. Responding quickly with its lead Operations Management Team, NorthStar was on site and configuring a plan of recovery within 6 hours of landfall. Crippled by a loss of power to all corners of the Polymers Plant, NorthStar quickly endeavored to bring power generation resources to bear to begin the recovery process. Quickly mobilizing manpower and resources, NorthStar accelerated its recovery efforts by implementing around the clock shift work and engaging a staff of over 100 personnel to expedite the reclamation, repair and restoration of all key industrial production facilities. From complex structural repairs, demolition of compromised engineering structures, environmental remediation efforts to the provisioning of a mobile office complex for Firestone staff, NorthStar enabled the commencement of production within an 23-day recovery effort, a testament to the efficacy of NorthStar- Firestone teamwork and efficiency.

projects.title: Former Dulski Federal Building
projects.summary: On-schedule delivery with no contract change orders. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, removed sprayed fireproofing, floor tile and mastic, interior partitions, and mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire-suppression systems. Work left the structural elements in place for the next stage of redevelopment. Demolition was sequenced to separate recyclable metals and masonry, with waste streams tracked throughout the work.
projects.overview: Downtown Buffalo is undergoing a comprehensive revitalize program. As part of that plan, Empire Dismantlement and Uniquest contracted LVI to abate asbestos-containing materials and demolish interior walls and MEP support systems of this 15-story, 400,000± square-foot former GSA Dulski office building. When the renovations are completed, the building will be a selfcontained multi-use office, hotel and condominium complex. Asbestos abatement work included sprayed-on fireproofing on the structural decks and steel members throughout the building and over 200,000 square feet of floor tile and mastic. Demolition included all interior modular partitions and other interior walls, excluding stairwells, shafts and electrical closets. LVI also demolished all mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire suppressions systems gutting each floor to just the structural elements. This work and the subsequent rebuild were a LEED project, requiring LVI to sequence demolition and segregate thousands of tons of waste that maximized recycling salvageable metals and clean masonry materials. Recyclable and non-salvageable waste streams were meticulously tracked and documented throughout the project. Approximately 7,200 tons of demolition materials were recycled including 7,004 tons of concrete and 200 tons of metals. LVI completed the entire scope safely, on schedule and without a single change order to the contract.

projects.title: Formosa Plastics Corporation
projects.summary: Hazardous-material response in a damaged chemical plant. NorthStar's scope included emergency debris cleanup, shoring of damaged buildings, hazardous-material handling and recovery of radioactive sources. Potential asbestos and chemical contamination shaped the approach. ATC performed sampling to identify contaminants and recommend remediation protocols, including protective equipment and waste-disposal requirements.
projects.overview:
In April 2004, an explosion rocked the Formosa Plastics Corporation plant in Illiopolis, IL. Debris from the explosion, mostly building materials and metal piping jacketing, scattered in all directions. Debris was found three miles away.

NorthStar, trained and licensed to handle hazardous materials, was contracted by Formosa Plastics Corporation to perform hazardous-material response work at the site. First, there was the emergency clean-up of debris strewn throughout the plant. All materials had to be assumed to be contaminated with asbestos and/or potentially hazardous chemicals. Radioactive sources needed recovery and proper recycling and plant buildings required shoring prior to remediation activities.

The actual chemical clean-up process was slow. A chemical lab that supported the plant was severely damaged by the explosion. In addition, toxic chemicals were formed through the heat and pressure created during the explosion and resultant fire. ATC conducted sampling to identify the type and concentration of chemicals present followed by a recommended remediation protocol which addressed personal protective equipment requirements and eventual disposal waste streams.

projects.title: Fortune 50 Major Retail Chain
projects.summary: Coordinated recovery for stores in multiple markets. Under a historical nationwide service agreement, NorthStar coordinated emergency response, water extraction, drying, mold remediation and selective demolition as required. Two assignments addressed tornado damage in Oklahoma City and hail damage in Carrollton, Georgia, including extensive roof-related water intrusion.
projects.overview:
NorthStar Recovery Services managed a Fortune 50 Major National Retailer with a Master Service Agreement on a national level. For all Emergency Response needs of the client, NorthStar was contacted by the client on a corporate level, then proceeded to work with the local manager of the facility once mobilized. Once an Emergency Response call was received, NRS mobilized equipment and crew within two hours and was on site within four hours, to facilitate any specific needs by the client.

NRS has responded to several isolated natural disasters for this Major Retail Chain providing emergen-cy response services, water extraction, moisture control & dehumidification, mold remediation, inte-rior & structural demolition and hazardous material removal as needed. Two examples are below:

Damage was caused by a tornado that struck one property in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The roof was punctured by the tornado’s winds, causing the property to incur severe debris and water dam-age. Over 75% of the property suffered water damage due to the damage of the roof. NorthStar provided debris removal, water extraction, drying, dehumidification, and post remediation services including anti-microbial and anti-bacterial wipe down.

Another property was damaged from a severe hail storm in Carrolton, Georgia. Similar to the dam-age in Oklahoma, the property had nearly 90% damage to the roof. NorthStar provided Emergency Response services including, debris removal, water extraction, drying and post remediation.

Both properties were complete within days of the disaster.

projects.title: Fortune 500 Multi-Family Housing
projects.summary: More than 1,200 housing units recovered in 14 days. NorthStar worked with the client's risk-management team before landfall, then mobilized resources to 25 damaged properties. Initial work addressed temporary power and dangerous debris, followed by water extraction, interior demolition, dehumidification and drying. More than 150 laborers supported the recovery effort.
projects.overview:
NorthStar Recovery Services managed a Fortune 500 Multi- Family Housing Corporation with a Master Service Agreement on a national level. Prior to Hurricane Ike, NRS identi-fied thirty five properties in the cone of hurricane probablility for the corporation in Houston, Texas. Before landfall of Hurricane Ike, NorthStar contacted the corporation’s risk management division and planned power provisions and equipment needs for the targeted properties in preparation for the storm.

Once Hurricane Ike made landfall, NorthStar mobilized equipment and manpower to twenty five of the properties damaged by the fierce hurricane. NorthStar’s initial response was for life safety issues such as power generation and dangerous debris removal. NorthStar Recovery Services provided temporary power generation, water extraction, interior demolition, dehumidification and drying for over twenty five properties. Over 1,200 units were safely recovered within fourteen days with crews of over 150 laborers.

projects.title: Fulton Learning Center
projects.summary: Ten classrooms supported recovery of a storm-damaged campus. NorthStar assessed the damage with roof specialists, tarped the building to limit further water entry, and deployed more than 20,000 CFM of desiccant drying equipment. Ten permanent mobile classrooms provided space for students whose regular classrooms needed the most extensive repairs.
projects.overview:
In August of 2017 Hurricane Harvey struck the Gulf Coast of Texas and caused significant widespread damage. Directly in the path of the hurricane was the city of Rockport, home to the Aransas County School District. One of the schools in the district, Fulton Learning Center, incurred a significant amount of damage as a result of the fierce winds and torrential rain brought on by Hurricane Harvey.

The extent of the damage was apparent shortly after the storm had passed, major water and wind damage and flooding across the entire campus. NorthStar first responders were on-site.

Damage assessments were conducted, and roof specialists were brought in to inspect the roof and assist with the formulation of a recovery plan. It was soon revealed that over 90% of the building’s roof had incurred major damage and would need replacement.

NorthStar crews got to work quickly and began the recovery process. The roof was tarped to prevent any further water intrusion and over 20,000CFM of desiccant drying equipment was employed to dry out the affected building materials. To allow school to resume as quickly as possible and prevent further academic delays, NorthStar installed 10 permanent mobile classrooms to accommodate students whose classrooms required the most significant repairs. In total, nearly 50% of the campus required some degree of reconstruction. After many months and over 17,000 working hours, major repairs and cleanup were completed and all that remained were minor finishing tasks.

projects.title: Hotel del Coronado
projects.summary: Historic-property upgrades while the hotel remained open. NorthStar removed selected interior finishes, structural components and exterior features, with asbestos and lead abatement as the work progressed. Management and supervision coordinated preservation requirements with an aggressive schedule, often using crews of more than 50 workers.
projects.overview:
From 1999 to 2012, NorthStar had a continuing presence at this century-old Victorian historic landmark "playground to the stars".

NorthStar's first task was selective demolition of interior finishes and structural components for a major seismic upgrade throughout the hotel. The scope of work also entailed the demolition of exterior flatwork and fixtures.

As the project progressed, asbestos and lead-based abatement and decontamination were constantly required. Many of the historical building components had to be preserved adding complexity to the project and requiring experienced management and supervision.

Throughout the project, the hotel remained open. NorthStar ensure that the project was sufficiently staffed to maintain an aggressive schedule. Crew size often exceeded fifty workers throughout the entire duration of the project.

NorthStar was also engaged for subsequent projects by the Hotel Del Coronado to continue updating the facility. Recently, as part of the hotel's remodeling plan, NorthStar was asked to perform asbestos and lead abatement in the spa, fitness center, and restaurant. NorthStar also performed the necessary demolition of the tennis courts to make room for the recently added Beach Village Cottages.

projects.title: Humboldt Bay Power Plant
projects.summary: Approximately 95% of removed materials recycled or salvaged. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, removed a 4,200-foot fuel-oil pipeline, cleaned and removed a 2.7-million-gallon tank, and cleared structures and utilities within the new facility footprint. Engineering hold points required crews to verify whether utilities were live before proceeding, supported by site-specific safety planning and twice-daily briefings.
projects.overview:
PG&E’s Humboldt Bay Power Plant (HBPP) is being re-powered to more efficiently meet California’s growing power needs. The 143-acre site has an interesting history that began in the early 1950’s where the local fishing industry and some agricultural lands were claimed for the building of a nuclear power plant. It operated from 1963-1976 when it went into SAFSTORE. However, the site continues to produce power using two fossil fuel plants.

LVI’s scope of work for the repowering effort was:

• Removing a shuttered, 4,200-linear-foot fuel oil pipeline that formerly conveyed fuel oil to the fossil units. • Cleaning, abating and removing a 2.7-million-gallon liquid fuel oil tank. • Demolishing and abating a series of structures, facilities, and underground utilities within the footprint of the new generation facilities.

The underground utilities posed a unique set of challenges. Record drawings of the subsurface conduit locations and the changes that had taken place over the last 50 years could not be located. As a result, the subsurface demolition had to be meticulously executed. Safety is always LVI’s first priority. A comprehensive Site-Specific Health and Safety Plan was written for the project. Work crews attended twice daily tailgate safety meetings to review potential job hazards and means and methods to mitigate the hazards.

Also, pre-project engineering evaluations and procedures included field “hold points” to identify and verify if utilities were ‘live’ so work crews would be safe and avoid disruption to plant operations.

The project also recycled or salvaged approximately 95% of the materials removed from the plant. This included 920 tons of concrete, 200 tons of asphalt, and 12 tons of metal debris.

Heavy winter rains did not hamper LVI’s expedited demolition and abatement activities.

During the project, as part of the community relations program, NorthStar utilized the Comprehensive Local Hiring Program and Community Friendly Diversity Supplier Participation Program to provide employment and training to the local area residents. Both Phase I and Phase II were completed by October 2009.

projects.title: Hunters Point Power Plant
projects.summary: Major material recovery from a constrained waterfront power site. NorthStar worked with TRC on boiler houses, turbines, tanks, administrative buildings and six tall stacks. Engineered crane dismantling reduced structures to approximately 50 feet before excavators completed the remaining removal. A subsequent contract addressed underground utility lines after the initial scope was finished.
projects.overview:
NorthStar worked with TRC Companies, Inc. on the decontamination and decommissioning of the Hunters Point Power Plant owned by Pacific Gas & Electric, in San Francisco, CA. The 38-acre site was positioned between two residential and commercial streets and the India Basin of San Francisco Bay. Surrounded on all sides by either water or infrastructure, it was among the most challenging D&D work ever undertaken by NorthStar. The project was also believed to be one of the largest fossil fuel utility sites that have gone through D&D in the United States.

The initial scope of work included complete asbestos abatement and demolition to grade of four boiler house units containing seven boilers; a back-up, jet-fueled turbine; a turbine house; storage tanks; administrative buildings; and six stacks ranging in height between 200 and 250 feet. The job was completed by a 60-employee union work force with 35% coming from the local community through the City Build Academy.

For the demolition work, NorthStar employed crane and excavator-engineered dismantling methods. Structures were dismantled to approximately 50 feet in height using cranes. The remaining portions were mechanically wrecked using excavators outfitted with hydraulic shears.

The project also had a major recycling component. Over a two-year period, the project generated 25,000 tons of steel, 30,000 tons of concrete, and approximately 75,000 gallons of oil for recycling and reuse.

After the initial scope of work was completed, NorthStar was awarded a second contract as PG&E prepared the site to be used for a community park. New work included removal of underground utility lines totaling approximately 25,000 linear feet. For this second contract, NorthStar maintained a workforce that included: 15 cross-trained demo/hazmat laborers, 5 foremen, 3 equipment operators, 1 Superintendent.

projects.title: Hurricane Sandy Recovery
projects.summary: Coordinated recovery across more than 200 facilities. NorthStar used advance weather intelligence to position resources, then coordinated temporary power, fuel, pumping, environmental controls, abatement, selective demolition and records recovery. Specialist trades worked across multiple locations, including sites where cranes were required to position generators.
projects.overview:
NorthStar responded and recovered over 200 commercial facilities including high-rise buildings, hotels, healthcare, industrial and retail facilities as well as university campuses damaged by Super Storm Sandy. The geographic area covered in the recovery effort included Western PA, Central and Northern NJ, NYC and Long Island.

NorthStar’s ability to respond quickly with labor, specialty equipment and overall expertise ensured our clients suffered the least possible damage as a result of this catastrophic, historic event. Our unique portfolio management program places substantial importance on proactively addressing critical areas of concern prior to an event. These proactive measures allowed our clients to be the first of the heavily damaged buildings in Manhattan to gain re-occupancy while others struggled with logistics.

NorthStar’s asset monitoring systems accurately identified our client’s critical facilities within the impact zone prior to Sandy making landfall. NorthStar’s private weather monitoring service and on staff meteorologist provided critical intelligence to facilitate sound decisions regarding the prepositioning of assets and reservation of specialty equipment.

Power Provisioning

As one of the largest power-loss events in our history, temporary power demand proved to be an enormous challenge. NorthStar successfully provided clients with all necessary power provisioning resources to facilitate the recovery effort during the initial response. Over 137 individual generators ranging from 800Kw to 2MW units were utilized throughout the impacted areas. Generator maintenance and fuel services were of critical importance to facilitating the stabilization and recovery of each property. Over 1.6 million gallons of fuel was consumed during the first few weeks of the effort. Limited access and lay down space in Manhattan complicated the mobilization of these large generator units. Cranes were utilized to lift many of the generators into position.

Labor Force

Massive labor forces comprised of multiple trades were required to perform the recovery effort at each of the damaged locations. NorthStar worked in excess of a quarter million man-hours with over 800 full time employees to ensure our clients recovered from this historic event. Multiple specialty trades worked in close coordination including operating engineers, environmental laborers, demolition experts and various other trade specialists providing the proper expertise for each discipline. into position.

Facilitating the pump out of millions of gallons of floodwater from lower levels of damaged buildings was second phase of the recovery effort. Common walls and up-stream pumping activities complicated the process. Large hydraulic pumps were submerged in the buildings below floating debris containing petroleum substances to effectively remove the seawater from the buildings.

Hazardous Material Management

NorthStar Group Services’ long history of environmental regulatory compliance assisted efforts to collaborate with environmental agencies to provide the most efficient and safest means of dealing with hazardous material contaminates in the floodwater. NorthStar worked with the New York City Department of Environmental Protection to design the process for containing and separating petroleum waste and other hazardous material from floodwaters. Other hazardous materials including asbestos were contained, abated, and disposed of per the local regulations. Accessing these materials in some locations required elaborate scaffolding. Damaged asbestos fireproofing was abated in many of the Manhattan high-rise buildings. Proper removal of all contaminates was carefully addressed to ensure the safety and integrity of all structures.

Shoring/Bracing and Demolition

Structural damage required shoring and bracing in many of the older buildings. Selective demolition of compromised building material, equipment, and furniture produced an immense amount of debris to be removed.

Debris Removal

In addition to floodwaters, thousands of tons of sand and mixed debris were excavated to gain access to multiple facilities on Coney Island and in Brooklyn. Heavy equipment including loaders, dump trucks, excavators and bobcats removed over 4,000 tons of mixed debris. Vehicles trapped in underground parking garages were lifted out and transported to off site locations for possessing.

Drying and Dehumidification

Trailer mounted desiccant dehumidification units and portable desiccants were utilized to remove residual moisture and re-establish environmental control within the affected structures. Drying activities were of critical importance to avoid further environmental and indoor air quality issues as well as secondary damage. Due to freezing temperatures, lack of temperature control during the initial stages of recovery further complicated the effort. To combat the freezing temperatures and possibility of pipe bursts, portable boilers and heating units were utilized.

Valuable Papers and Records

NorthStar processed in excess of 8,500 cubic feet of valuable papers and records from various facilities.

Notable Project During Hurricane Sandy

Long Beach Medical Center

NorthStar was engaged by the Director of Facilities for Long Beach Medical Center to provide Critical recovery services in the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy. As a result of the storm, the entire basement level of the facility had taken on over 12 feet of water and associated debris. Coincidentally, all of the electrical, mechanical, and HVAC equipment was located in the central plant within the basement of the facility. Significant services for the hospital including Administration, Pharmacy, Kitchen, and Laundry were also severely affected.

A scope of work was quickly established and NorthStar began implementing measures to regain interior environmental control of the facility and mitigate any further damage, including bringing in temporary power and large-scale desiccant dehumidification. Once the water had been pumped out of the basement, medical records were removed, recovered, and disposed of. Along with a significant amount of debris brought in by the flood water, there was approximately 3 feet of sand and silt that had accumulated which was removed as well.

At the projects end, the total cost exceeded $18 million and took nearly 2 years. Additionally, this was yet another project conducted by NorthStar that resulted in zero OSHA recordable injuries.

Our unique portfolio management program places substantial importance on proactively addressing critical areas of concern prior to an event. These proactive measures allowed our clients to be the first of the heavily damaged buildings in Manhattan to gain re-occupancy while others struggled with logistics.

NorthStar’s asset monitoring systems accurately identified our client’s critical facilities within the impact zone prior to Sandy making landfall. NorthStar’s private weather monitoring service and on staff meteorologist provided critical intelligence to facilitate sound decisions regarding the prepositioning of assets and reservation of specialty equipment.

Power Provisioning

As one of the largest power-loss events in our history, temporary power demand proved to be an enormous challenge. NorthStar successfully provided clients with all necessary power provisioning resources to facilitate the recovery effort during the initial response. Over 137 individual generators ranging from 800Kw to 2MW units were utilized throughout the impacted areas. Generator maintenance and fuel services were of critical importance to facilitating the stabilization and recovery of each property. Over 1.6 million gallons of fuel was consumed during the first few weeks of the effort. Limited access and lay down space in Manhattan complicated the mobilization of these large generator units. Cranes were utilized to lift many of the generators into position.

Labor Force

Massive labor forces comprised of multiple trades were required to perform the recovery effort at each of the damaged locations. NorthStar worked in excess of a quarter million man-hours with over 800 full time employees to ensure our clients recovered from this historic event. Multiple specialty trades worked in close coordination including operating engineers, environmental laborers, demolition experts and various other trade specialists providing the proper expertise for each discipline. into position.

Facilitating the pump out of millions of gallons of floodwater from lower levels of damaged buildings was second phase of the recovery effort. Common walls and up-stream pumping activities complicated the process. Large hydraulic pumps were submerged in the buildings below floating debris containing petroleum substances to effectively remove the seawater from the buildings.

Hazardous Material Management

NorthStar Group Services’ long history of environmental regulatory compliance assisted efforts to collaborate with environmental agencies to provide the most efficient and safest means of dealing with hazardous material contaminates in the floodwater. NorthStar worked with the New York City Department of Environmental Protection to design the process for containing and separating petroleum waste and other hazardous material from floodwaters. Other hazardous materials including asbestos were contained, abated, and disposed of per the local regulations. Accessing these materials in some locations required elaborate scaffolding. Damaged asbestos fireproofing was abated in many of the Manhattan high-rise buildings. Proper removal of all contaminates was carefully addressed to ensure the safety and integrity of all structures.

Shoring/Bracing and Demolition

Structural damage required shoring and bracing in many of the older buildings. Selective demolition of compromised building material, equipment, and furniture produced an immense amount of debris to be removed.

Debris Removal

In addition to floodwaters, thousands of tons of sand and mixed debris were excavated to gain access to multiple facilities on Coney Island and in Brooklyn. Heavy equipment including loaders, dump trucks, excavators and bobcats removed over 4,000 tons of mixed debris. Vehicles trapped in underground parking garages were lifted out and transported to off site locations for possessing.

Drying and Dehumidification

Trailer mounted desiccant dehumidification units and portable desiccants were utilized to remove residual moisture and re-establish environmental control within the affected structures. Drying activities were of critical importance to avoid further environmental and indoor air quality issues as well as secondary damage. Due to freezing temperatures, lack of temperature control during the initial stages of recovery further complicated the effort. To combat the freezing temperatures and possibility of pipe bursts, portable boilers and heating units were utilized.

Valuable Papers and Records

NorthStar processed in excess of 8,500 cubic feet of valuable papers and records from various facilities.

Notable Project During Hurricane Sandy

Long Beach Medical Center

NorthStar was engaged by the Director of Facilities for Long Beach Medical Center to provide Critical recovery services in the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy. As a result of the storm, the entire basement level of the facility had taken on over 12 feet of water and associated debris. Coincidentally, all of the electrical, mechanical, and HVAC equipment was located in the central plant within the basement of the facility. Significant services for the hospital including Administration, Pharmacy, Kitchen, and Laundry were also severely affected.

A scope of work was quickly established and NorthStar began implementing measures to regain interior environmental control of the facility and mitigate any further damage, including bringing in temporary power and large-scale desiccant dehumidification. Once the water had been pumped out of the basement, medical records were removed, recovered, and disposed of. Along with a significant amount of debris brought in by the flood water, there was approximately 3 feet of sand and silt that had accumulated which was removed as well.

At the projects end, the total cost exceeded $18 million and took nearly 2 years. Additionally, this was yet another project conducted by NorthStar that resulted in zero OSHA recordable injuries.
