projects.title: Iowa Avian Influenza Response
projects.summary: Biosecure disposal and cleanup across 13 poultry farms. NorthStar organized disposal through landfill, incineration and composting, followed by farm-structure cleanout and decontamination. Vehicle, container and personnel procedures addressed loading sites, transport stages and disposal locations. More than 100 workers supported the operation.
projects.overview:
In 2015 several Chicken and Turkey farm facilities in Iowa were infected with a deadly Bird Influenza that resulted in the deaths of millions of poultry birds. NorthStar Recovery Services was contacted to handle the disposal of the bird carcasses at 13 of these farms.

NorthStar first responders arrived on-site and began developing a plan to dispose of the deceased birds with a primary focus on Biological Security and Infection Control. Decontamination protocols were implemented for both vehicles transporting the infected birds as well as personnel working in and around the contaminated areas.

The entire project was conducted in two phases. Disposal of the Deceased Birds. Disposal was conducted via three methods: landfill dumping, incineration, and composting.

Clean-out and Decontamination of Farm Structures. Decontamination of trucks and their containers was conducted both at the facility where the biological debris was loaded as well as at the dump site to prevent biological contamination during transport. A very rigorous three-part decontamination protocol was implemented to ensure that biological hazards were eliminated prior to each stage of travel.

In total, NorthStar Recovery Services made over 1000 truckload runs-approximately 50 per day-to various disposal sites. By the end of the project, over 13 million chicken and turkey carcasses had been removed and disposed of. A workforce of over 100 laborers was employed throughout the project with zero safety incidents or OSHA recordable injuries. NorthStar worked closely with the EPA and exceeded protocols for Biological Security, ultimately resulting in a safe and efficient recovery process.

projects.overview:
NorthStar Recovery Services had a Master Service Agreement with Jones Lang LaSalle and HSBC to cover their entire National portfolio. NorthStar responded daily to JLL/HSBC throughout the country for fire, water and disaster recovery.

NorthStar recovered multiple HSBC properties after Super Storm Sandy and worked alongside Jones Lang LaSalle in the days leading up to the storm; providing 2 weather updates per day with on staff meteorologist. NRS most recently responded to multiple pipe breaks at various HSBC locations in the Northeast as a result of the Polar Vortex. NRS is able to respond to multiple sites at the same time; ensuring minimal downtime after a regional event that effects more than one facility.

projects.title: Kmart Guayama
projects.summary: Receiving and stock areas operational within four months. NorthStar assessed the structure with engineers and electricians, secured the building, installed shoring and a temporary separation wall, and removed damaged HVAC systems and roof debris. Local and mainland vendors supplied labor and equipment while crews remediated microbial growth across the building.
projects.overview:
In the wake of Hurricane Maria, the Island of Puerto Rico sustained extensive catastrophic damage. One of NorthStar’s longest standing clients, Sears Holdings, had multiple stores affected, one of which was a Kmart in the city of Guayama. Due to the heavy rain and winds, a large portion of the roof on this store had collapsed. NorthStar was called to respond to this loss and began allocating manpower and resources. Once NorthStar gained access to Puerto Rico and the surrounding devastation, two lead Project Managers responded to the loss site to begin the damage assessment, drafting of the initial scope of work, and procurement of resources.

The scope of work was sizeable and included the following: board-up and security of the building, installation of shoring on the interior of the building for stabilization of the structure, construction of a temporary wall to separate the collapsed roof area from the rest of the building, continued control of water intrusion from the collapsed section of roof, removal of destroyed HVAC systems and roof debris, and finally the remediation of the entire building for microbial growth. However, before any work could begin NorthStar engaged electricians and engineers and completed tasks that would ensure the safety of the structure.

NorthStar worked with both local and U.S. mainland-based vendors to procure labor and equipment for this project. Large equipment used on this project included a generator, skid steer, multiple scissor lifts, 2 large cranes, and various sized dumpsters. At its peak the project employed 25 laborers for one 12-hour shift. Over the course of 30,000+ man hours worked on this project, there were zero OSHA recordable injuries.

Several challenges were overcome throughout the duration of this project. Two major hurricanes had passed through Puerto Rico within a span of just 30 days causing mass power outages and restricting access to even the most rudimentary resources such as potable water and functional plumbing. In light of these difficulties, NorthStar was able to remediate over 150,000 square feet of building space and have 75% of the sales floor and 100% of the receiving and merchandise stock area operational in just 4 months.

projects.title: Lazarus Building
projects.summary: Selective demolition supporting reuse of a historic landmark. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, performed demolition for Turner Construction and abatement for Clayton Group Services. Crews gutted seven floors, a basement and subbasement; removed elevators; and addressed a wide range of asbestos-containing and other regulated materials. One elevator cab was carefully preserved at the historical society's request.
projects.overview:
LVI was contracted by Turner Construction Co. for the demolition portion of the project. Clayton Group Services contracted LVI for the abatement work involved with the renovation of this 1,000,000 square-foot former retail store. Selective demolition occurred on all 7 floors plus a basement and sub basement. The building received a complete interior gut. In addition, LVI was tasked with the removal of all elevators in the building. The historical society requested that one of the elevator cabs be preserved for re-erection. Special care was taken to provide them with a complete undamaged cab. The original abatement contract was for approximately 23,000 lineal feet of pipe insulation, 2800 fittings, 167,000 square feet of tile and mastic, 100 fire doors, 50,000 lineal feet of electrical wiring, 6500 glue dots, 350 square feet of duct insulation, 15,000 bulbs, 7500 ballasts and 2700 square feet of transite. These quantities increased significantly through 129 change orders.

This 100-year old landmark in downtown Columbus became a model of “green renovations” and was award LEED gold certification.

projects.title: Long Beach Medical Center
projects.summary: Stabilization of a flood-damaged healthcare facility. NorthStar and the facility team established a stabilization scope. Work included interior environmental control, handling and recovery of medical records, and disposal of damaged pharmaceuticals. NorthStar continued ambient control while the hospital and FEMA considered the future of key building systems.
projects.overview:
December, 2012, Long Beach Medical Center called on NorthStar after taking on 12 feet of water in the basement area which, housed all electrical and mechanical equipment including boilers as well as HVAC to the hospital. Administration, Pharmacy, Kitchen and Laundry Services were severely affected as well.

Once scope of work was developed by both parties, NorthStar provided stabilization of the entire facility as well as removal and recovery of medical records and the proper disposing of all damaged pharmaceuticals.

NorthStar continued to provide Ambient Control to the entire facility pending a decision by the Hospital and FEMA to re-locate and provide new HVAC, Mechanical and Electrical Systems.

projects.title: LSU Student Health Center
projects.summary: East-wing services resumed after two weeks. NorthStar removed debris and hazardous material, cleared contents, and performed ice blasting, duct cleaning, odor mitigation and equipment restoration. The team also cleaned, disinfected and deodorized the more heavily affected wing to prepare it for reconstruction.
projects.overview:
The LSU Student Health Center on Infirmary Dr. plays a critical role in student life on campus. An electrical fire began in the ceiling of the facility which left the west wing destroyed and the east wing unusable due to the heavy amount of smoke damage. NorthStar responded to support recovery after the fire.

Due to the significant amount of structural damage, NorthStar began by removing debris and other hazardous materials before moving on to clear out the structure’s contents which included medical supplies, office equipment and electronics. Once the area was cleared, our team began the restoration process of ice blasting, duct cleaning, odor mitigation and equipment restoration.

After only 2 weeks, the university was able to reopen the east wing of the facility which resumed helping students immediately. By the end of July, our team had cleaned, disinfected and deodorized the more heavily affected west wing preparing it for reconstruction so that the full facility would be in use in time for the fall semester. Additionally, our team of equipment restoration specialists were able to restore a majority of the computers affected by the fire which meant securing critical medical data that otherwise would have been lost.

projects.title: LSU Tabletop Exercise
projects.summary: Campus teams rehearsed recovery before a loss. NorthStar developed a scenario at the Chemical & Materials Building and worked through the response with LSU risk management, facilities, utilities, emergency management and other campus teams. U.S. Data Wing performed drone surveys of two rooftops as part of the wider preparation program.
projects.overview:
February 2018 was a busy time in the NorthStar Business Continuity Division’s schedule. The team was involved in meetings with multiple LSU departments with the goal of organizing both Phase I of the Pre-Loss Assessments on the campus, a drone survey demonstration, as well as NorthStar’s first “Table Top Exercise”.

The execution of the PLA’s on the campus as well as the drone survey were scheduled and executed without a hitch. The PLA team was able to complete all objectives as well as a few properties in addition to those scheduled for Phase I.

The First Tabletop is a Huge Success

U.S. Data Wing performed the drone surveys flawlessly and provided LSU with incredibly detailed information of two of their building rooftops. Once the information was delivered to LSU, NorthStar’s focus was set on the upcoming table top exercise.

The main event was the table top exercise that took place on February 27th. Personnel from several of LSU’s main departments were present: Risk Management, Facilities Services, Utilities Services, Facilities Maintenance, Emergency Management, and Contracts & Elevators. NorthStar was also present in force with team members from Operations, Business Development, and Business Continuity.

The scenario for this exercise was developed by NorthStar and centered around a fire/water loss at the Chemical & Materials Building. Once the exercise had begun, NorthStar Operations personnel worked well in concert with LSU staff to walk through the loss response and recovery process. In the end, it was obvious that the relationship between LSU and NorthStar had been strengthened.

"The underwriters were impressed by the amount of work that has been put in toward the development of pre-loss assessments. SOP’s, and planning”, wrote the Assistant Director of Risk Management at LSU. It was also expressed that LSU is very impressed with NorthStar’s commitment to “provide both people and resources for minor and major losses that may impact campus.”

The NorthStar Business Continuity Division expects that several more clients will be scheduling table top exercises in the following months. The benefits of running a table top exercise have drawn interest from a wide array of clients, from universities to manufacturing plants.

projects.title: Major Theme Park Fire
projects.summary: Fire cleanup completed while the park remained open. NorthStar removed fire-damaged debris across more than eight acres of the site. Work addressed materials including asbestos, lead, heavy metals and vehicle fluids, requiring controlled handling within an operating entertainment property.
projects.overview:
In 2008, a fast-moving fire exploded on a major theme park in southern California. Many movie sets for attractions were destroyed as a result of the fire. The fire burned about two city blocks and affected about three and a half acres of the 391-acre park.

NorthStar Recovery Services provided debris clean-up of fire damaged buildings for over eight acres of the site. Many of the buildings contained hazardous materials such as asbestos, lead, heavy metals and vehicle fluids. Because of the publicity of the fire, all work was completed under high security while the park was open to the public. This job was completed on schedule and without incident.

projects.title: Matagorda County Courthouse
projects.summary: Courthouse operations continued during recovery. NorthStar provided temporary power and smoke-and-soot removal, scheduling night and weekend shifts to reduce disruption. Daily updates helped the facilities team coordinate scheduled activities and multiple trades. The work also included installation of a permanent backup-generation system.
projects.overview:
NorthStar Recovery Services managed the Matagorda County Courthouse under a Master Services Agreement to provide services for any emergency and environmental issues experienced at the site.

Following an electrical fire, NorthStar was called upon to respond to the courthouse after significant damage to the structure and contents. NorthStar provided temporary power, smoke and soot removal services. The extent of damage spanned all three floors of the building's interior as well as significant portions of the exterior.

Due to the immediate response of NorthStar, business within the courthouse was able to continue. To minimize any business interruption, temporary power was deployed as well as night and weekend shifts to accomplish the scope of work quickly and efficiently. In addition, NorthStar performed the installation of a new, permanent backup power generation system.

NorthStar daily updates allowed the courthouse facilities team to accommodate scheduled activities with accuracy. Consistent project management allowed multiple trades to work in concert to accomplish the goals of the project. NorthStar's professionalism and experience resulted in the project being completed both on schedule and within the budget provided.

projects.title: Navy CBC Barracks
projects.summary: Two Gulfport barracks completed in four days. NorthStar worked around the clock at Gulfport, expanding from one barracks to a second. At Key West, the requested workforce grew from 50 to 300. Crews coordinated with KBR, NAVFAC and the industrial hygienist on abatement, remediation and housing turnover.
projects.overview:
CBC Gulfport: The job began as carpet removal in one 3-story barracks. The barracks had asbestoscontaining tile under the carpet that needed to be removed. The schedule on this project was critical. These barracks had to be completed and turned over to the Navy in two weeks. Our crews worked around the clock to accommodate the accelerated schedule and by the second day on base we had positioned ourselves to perform work on another barracks with the same issues and schedule.

NorthStar completed both buildings in four days and this caught the attention of the project managers and program general manager. One week into the project the project manager for KBR requested 75 men until the project was completed. We performed work in various buildings and in the Navy housing units on base. We completed asbestos removal in the roofing systems on several buildings.

KBR NAS Key West: The CONCAP Program General Manager contacted NorthStar to mobilize 50 men to respond to the NAS Key West be-cause of damage caused by Hurricane Wilma. One day after the initial contact, the labor force was increased to 100 men. The NAS in Key West received approximately one foot of water throughout many buildings on the four annexes along with damage to 700 Navy housing units. Once mobilized, NorthStar was again requested to increase its labor force, this time to 300. We performed work in several buildings, including one building that required a very high security level. The bulk of our work was performed in the Navy housing units, with the work concentrated on Sigsbee Park. Approximately 70% of the houses damaged had asbestos and mold issues. We were the only certified and licensed contractor to perform this type of work for KBR. NorthStar worked closely with KBR, NAVFAC and the CIH to provide quality, safe and timely turnover of the houses to begin the put back work.

projects.title: NRG Dunkirk Power Plant
projects.summary: Abatement completed within the scheduled outage. NorthStar abated exhaust ducts, defunct precipitators, hot-air crossover ducts, induced-draft fan ducts and air heaters. Crew sizes reached 60 people to support the schedule. The team also subcontracted re-insulation work as part of the coordinated scope.
projects.overview:
The oldest coal-fired units at this station have been running since 1950; the others since 1959 and 1960. NRG undertook a plant-wide emissions program that would be more environmentally friendly and provide more reliable sources of energy to New York State.

NorthStar was asked to abate the exhaust ducts to the old precipitators, defunct cold box precipitators, hot air crossover ducts, ID fan ducts and air heaters. NorthStar subcontracted the re-insulation work. To complete the work during a scheduled outage, crew sizes were as high as 60 people. Ambient temperatures went as high as 140˚F. All work was finished on schedule with no OSHA recordables and no regulatory violations.

projects.title: Nucla Power Plant
projects.summary: Integrated abatement adapted to changing site conditions. NorthStar combined demolition and asbestos-removal capabilities across four work areas. Crews removed more than 130,000 square feet of exterior asbestos siding, managed approximately 250 cubic feet of vermiculite and packaged about 700 cubic yards of asbestos waste. The team obtained a Colorado variance for the specified Unit 4 implosion method.
projects.overview:
The Scope of Work included the removal of the exterior asbestos siding in excess of 130,000 SF from both the Boiler 1- 3 building and Boiler 3 building. NorthStar obtained a variance from the CDPHE to allow for the implosion of unit 4 with asbestos containing materials left in place. NorthStar performed the removal and management of approximately 250 cubic feet of vermiculite. NorthStar also collected, packaged and loaded approximately 700 cubic yards of asbestos containing waste from the plant for transportation and disposal. Due to NorthStar’s ability to perform both asbestos abatement and demolition, we were able to perform the abatement and demolition with little schedule adjustment when additional asbestos containing materials were discovered after the decommissioning started.

The general scope of work for this project consisted of the thermal cutting of boiler breeching and removal of asbestos containing materials, regulated building materials, and universal waste from the 4 boiler units and precipitators, and complete demolition of all structures at the Nucla Power Plant. The abatement locations were completed in four phases Boilers 1-3, Boiler 4, precipitators, and exterior siding removal.

The Nucla Power Plant was located in a very remote area. The property is slated for reuse by Tri-State.

projects.title: NYU Law Administration Building
projects.summary: Controlled urban demolition with a 90% recycling result. NorthStar/Mazzocchi used engineered shoring and bracing, strict vibration monitoring and hand demolition down to grade. Mechanical demolition followed at the basement and cellar levels. The approach addressed the constraints of the busy West Village street and the theater's retained perimeter walls.
projects.overview:
NorthStar/Mazzocchi was contracted to perform the demolition of the NYU Law Administration Building at 133 MacDougal Street in New York City to make way for the construction of a new administration building for NYU’s Law School. The five-story building, of wood frame construction, had a brick façade which unified the structure of the building. Originally, the building had been constructed as four consecutive brownstone residences, which had been converted into a combination of residential and office use. Additionally, the first floor and basement level of one of the brownstones housed the Provincetown Playhouse, with portions of the building dating back to the early 1800s.

To meet obligations to the neighborhood, NYU required that the four perimeter walls of the first floor and basement level of the playhouse be maintained. The intent of salvaging these walls was to incorporate and refurbish the playhouse for use after the new administration building is constructed.

The project was located on an extremely busy residential street of NYU’s campus located in the West Village of New York City, which presented many challenges. The adjacent building to the south, a fully occupied mixed use commercial and residential building, was over 100 years old and leaning against the building to be demolished. This necessitated a fully engineered shoring and bracing plan to protect the building. The adjacent building to the north was a fully occupied residential building, and also required shoring and bracing. NorthStar adhered to very strict vibration monitoring standards, due to the requirements of the client and their consultants, to protect these adjacent structures.

Actual demolition consisted of hand demolition down to grade level, and then use of mechanical means for demolition of the basement and cellar levels and load-out of materials. The project was fully compliant with all NYC rules and regulations. Additionally, this was a LEED project with 90% recycling goals, which were achieved. All work on the project was completed without any safety incidents.

projects.title: Odyssey After School
projects.summary: School recovery delivered with zero OSHA recordables. NorthStar assessed the damage with roof specialists and carried out roof replacement, asbestos abatement, mold remediation, debris removal, interior demolition and reconstruction. The team installed two new portable classrooms and supported the work with a 500 kW generator and a 175-ton crane.
projects.overview:
August of 2017 was a difficult time for the city of Rockport, Texas. Hurricane Harvey made landfall directly upon this small Gulf Coast town and caused widespread damage across the region. The Odyssey After School facility, part of the Aransas County School District, was one of the buildings in the area that was heavily impacted by the extreme winds and torrential rains that accompanied Hurricane Harvey. Students and faculty were left with an unusable facility and began to question weather or not the school year would be able to resume. Once NorthStar arrived on-site it was clear that full recovery was well within reach and that the school year would not be a total loss.

The school had incurred major roof damage which subsequently led to significant interior water intrusion. Many parts of the school were heavily saturated with water and on the verge of succumbing to even worse secondary damage. In addition to the main facility, mobile classrooms located on the campus were heavily damaged and rendered unusable as a result.

Once on site, NorthStar teams performed damage assessments and engaged roof inspection specialists. Further inspection resulted in the determination that the entire roof of the facility would have to be replaced. As the project progressed NorthStar performed many additional activities while working towards a full recovery for the school, including Asbestos abatement, mold remediation, extensive debris cleanup, interior demolition and reconstruction, and the installation of two brand new portable classrooms. To assist with the completion of required tasks, NorthStar procured a 500kW generator and a 175Ton crane, both of which remained on-site throughout the duration of the project. The labor crew headed by NorthStar logged in more than 20,500 working hours before reaching project completion, with zero OSHA recordable injuries.

sections.heading: Project story
sections.text:
August of 2017 was a difficult time for the city of Rockport, Texas. Hurricane Harvey made landfall directly upon this small Gulf Coast town and caused widespread damage across the region. The Odyssey After School facility, part of the Aransas County School District, was one of the buildings in the area that was heavily impacted by the extreme winds and torrential rains that accompanied Hurricane Harvey. Students and faculty were left with an unusable facility and began to question weather or not the school year would be able to resume. Once NorthStar arrived on-site it was clear that full recovery was well within reach and that the school year would not be a total loss.

The school had incurred major roof damage which subsequently led to significant interior water intrusion. Many parts of the school were heavily saturated with water and on the verge of succumbing to even worse secondary damage. In addition to the main facility, mobile classrooms located on the campus were heavily damaged and rendered unusable as a result.

Once on site, NorthStar teams performed damage assessments and engaged roof inspection specialists. Further inspection resulted in the determination that the entire roof of the facility would have to be replaced. As the project progressed NorthStar performed many additional activities while working towards a full recovery for the school, including Asbestos abatement, mold remediation, extensive debris cleanup, interior demolition and reconstruction, and the installation of two brand new portable classrooms. To assist with the completion of required tasks, NorthStar procured a 500kW generator and a 175Ton crane, both of which remained on-site throughout the duration of the project. The labor crew headed by NorthStar logged in more than 20,500 working hours before reaching project completion, with zero OSHA recordable injuries.

projects.title: Pentagon Renovations
projects.summary: Four million square feet of work with critical systems maintained. NorthStar Group Services performed more than four million square feet of abatement and demolition across Wedges II–V. The team removed hazardous materials and nonstructural components, separated occupied areas with barriers, coordinated tenant movements and scheduled major system work during off-peak periods.
projects.overview:
The goal of the Pentagon renovation program was to upgrade the Pentagon into a modern, flexible and safe military command environment that will endure well into the 21st Century. This project involved the complete abatement of hazardous materials including lead, PCB and mercury in addition to the demolition of interior architectural building components and all mechanical, electrical, plumbing and telecommunication systems.

NGS (NorthStar Group Services) began work in early 2001 and completed over 4,000,000 square feet of abatement and demolition on Wedges II, III, IV and V. The project will be completed in early 2011. The entire abatement and demolition package is valued at over $80,000,000 with options. Each wedge contract was awarded separately and NGS is proud to have been selected for each subsequent contract.

Services: Critical elements of the work performed include complex decommissioning of operational security and telecommunication systems, mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems. NGS demolished all non-structural, architectural building components and removed them from the building utilizing both manual and mechanical demolition methods.

NGS removed over 40,000 tons of hazardous waste. Construction debris was segregated for reusable metals, concrete, brick, and other building components under the USGBC LEED Program.

Safety & Security: All personnel were required to undergo background checks. For the duration of the project, NGS was required to coordinate the loading of debris and the movement of material through an intense security apparatus, inspecting both the interior and exterior of every vehicle requiring site access. NGS was given access to the site through the Pentagon’s Remote Delivery Facility. During the course of deconstruction activities, NGS segregated active work site areas from occupied areas via construction of hard wall and dust barriers, notifying and re-routing tenants, and by posting signage. NGS continually monitored the work zone and adjacent public spaces to minimize dust and debris.

Scheduling & Timeline: Each contract was completed using phased project scheduling. For example, Wedges II & III involved the selective demolition of MEP systems while maintaining critical components of the systems passing through the work zones. As the result of our efforts, no MEP system interruptions resulted due to NGS’s work. The project had to be completed according to the master schedule developed by the Pentagon Renovation Team. The schedule took into account relocation of tenants, as needed, and the necessity for the facility to remain fully operational 24/7 in support of military operations. Major decommissioning requirements were handled during off-peak hours, weekends and holidays to allow for uninterrupted building services. Staffing & Project Management: Our management team included one senior project manager, one general superintendent, two full-time safety managers, two superintendents and ten foremen. NGS utilized both mechanical and manual demolition and abatement methods while employing up to 200 full-time employees and 70 sub-contractor employees. NGS exceeded minority participation goals of 26% and subcontracting goals of 33% to WBE, SDB and MBE firms for all work. 9-11-01: NGS was already on-site when the 9/11 hit the Pentagon. NGS provided emergency response services and was able to assist the Pentagon in maintaining mission critical services.

projects.title: Public Storage Houston
projects.summary: Full facility operation restored within one week. The recovery team extracted water, sanitized common areas and dried the affected building. Each unit was opened and inspected. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, assisted tenants with temporarily relocating contents, separating items for disposal, sanitizing storage spaces and returning salvaged belongings.
projects.overview:
NorthStar was contracted by Public Storage to respond to a water loss resulting from a sprinkler head that had been damaged by a vandal on the top floor of the 3-story facility. The leak affected all three floors where over 400 rental units were located.

The scope of work initially included water extraction and sanitation of the main hallways and walls, along with drying and dehumidification of the entire affected area.

Individual storage units were then opened and inspected for damages. Those units that were affected were then emptied of contents so that each unit could be dried and sanitized. LVI assisted each rental unit tenant as needed to re-locate contents to a temporary location, segregate unwanted contents for disposal, sanitize each storage unit, and then move the salvaged contents back into the sanitized storage units. There were ultimately over 200 units that had been affected. Additionally, LVI communicated with the rental unit clients to provide a calm and orderly atmosphere during the entire process, and was commended by Public Storage for doing so.

The entire facility was restored to full operation within one week. Public Storage management compared this situation to a previous similar one that had been handled by another contractor, and concluded that LVI’s one-week completion time compared with a one-month completion time by the other contractor, and at one-half the cost.

projects.title: Regional Pool Alliance & Aransas County
projects.facility: School District Facilities and Municipal Buildings
projects.summary: Approximately 80 buildings recovered within a 12-month program. NorthStar arrived within 12 hours of the storm passing to assess conditions and develop scopes. Pre-loss assessments supported planning. Crews prioritized schools, provided drying and temporary power, rebuilt roofs and interiors, and converted a vacant retail space into temporary courthouse accommodation.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Harvey made landfall near Rockport, Texas, on August 25, 2017. The storm caused extensive damage across Aransas County and surrounding communities.

Two NorthStar clients, Aransas County and Regional Pool Alliance, an alliance of three school districts, experienced significant damage across their facilities. Air handlers were torn from rooftops, windows were broken and water damage was extensive. NorthStar was on site within 12 hours of the storm passing to survey damage and develop scopes of work.

Approximately 80 buildings required recovery work, including schools and municipal facilities. Roof damage allowed water into many buildings. The county courthouse was severely damaged and slated for replacement; other affected facilities included the airport.

NorthStar mobilized drying equipment, temporary power and a substantial workforce. At the county judge's request, schools were prioritized. Work included interior drying, debris removal, cleaning, emergency reconstruction and roof rebuilding. The program reports that Taft and Ingleside schools resumed on September 16 and Aransas County schools on October 10.

NorthStar converted a vacant retail property into temporary courthouse accommodation while a new courthouse was planned and constructed. The company's scope combined cleanup, drying, demolition and reconstruction. More than $100 million of recovery work was completed within 12 months, on time and with zero accidents reported.

Pre-loss assessments conducted several months before Harvey supported the response. Photo documentation, floor plans, site plans and other facility information helped define the work and coordinate the recovery.

projects.overview:
NDA members NorthStar Contracting Group and Controlled Demolition, Inc. worked together to demolish and implode, respectively, the structures that made up the 26-acre campus of the Riviera Hotel and Casino. Four total buildings were imploded, including the Monaco Tower, Monte Carlo Tower, South Tower, and the South Tower Expansion. 17 other buildings were demolished manually.

The historic hotel and casino was the first highrise hotel on the Las Vegas Strip and was also the backdrop for several big-name Hollywood films. In May of 2015, after 60 years in operation, "The Riv" was closed for good to make way for an expansion of the Las Vegas Convention Center.

The Demolition project was conducted via three methods. The interior of the buildings were first stripped of all hazardous materials, including asbestos, PCB ballasts, mercury light tubes, neon, and much more. Work areas where asbestos containing materials were beging removed were cordoned off with the proper levels of containment and utilized the best procedures for dust management. The removed materials were properly packaged, manifested, and disposed of in accordance with federal, state, and local laws and regulations and secured on-site prior to transport to an approved debris collection facility.

The exterior and larger demolition procedures were conducted via four teams of two large excavators, each mounted with various tools. Using a combination of steel shears, crushers, breakers, and stinger attachments, the excavators were able to systematically dismantle the structures both safely and efficiently.

The third method of demolition was implosion. NorthStar enlisted the assistance of Controlled Demolition Inc. to perform both Phase I and II of the procedure which was conducted on Monaco and Monte Carlo towers.

projects.overview:
NorthStar Recovery Services managed Sears Holdings under a Master Service Agreement on a national level for all Emergency Response needs. NorthStar was contacted by the client on a corporate level, then proceeded to work with the local manager of the facility once mobilized. NorthStar mobilized equipment and crew within two hours and was on site within four hours to facilitate any specific needs.

NorthStar responded to every weather event that has impacted Sears Holdings assets during an eight-year service period. Services provided to Sears Holdings include but are not limited to water extraction, moisture control & dehumidification, mold remediation, interior & structural demolition and hazardous material removal.

projects.title: St. John's University
projects.summary: Three-day remediation enabled critical systems repairs. NorthStar deployed generators, cabling and electricians, maintained fuel and equipment around the clock, and supplied gasoline for campus vehicles. At Manhattan, more than 25 remediation personnel extracted contaminated water, removed debris, dried structures and cleaned the approximately 10,000-square-foot physical plant.
projects.overview:
Upon making landfall in the New York Metropolitan Area on October 29, 2012, Superstorm Sandy caused extended power outages to all campuses as well as significant flooding affecting the Manhattan campus main building and specifically the physical plant operating the campus. The primary concern was the safety, well-being and comfort of the 3200 Resident Students as well as faculty and staff remaining on campus during and after the storm. Additionally, the resumption of full university operations as well as the continuity of operation of critical and delicate scientific research facilities and activities were also of paramount importance.

As the principal facilities emergency response provider for SJU at the time of Sandy’s landfall, Northstar deployed the following:

• 8 generator sets ranging from 175KW to 1.25 MW providing power to the dormitories, science complex, law school and other academic, administrative and event facilities. • Approximately 3000 feet of cabling and associated connections. • Over 20 electricians to provide and maintain temporary power for all campuses under the direction of SJU facilities engineering. • All fuel and equipment maintenance to maintain constant 24/7 operations. At the Manhattan Campus, NRS performed class III black water extraction, structural drying, cleaning, decontamination and sanitizing of the critical infrastructure of an approximately 10,000 square foot physical plant facility In view of the displaced Manhattan Campus resident students, a timetable for the return of resident students needed be established, highlighting the importance of rapid completion of the restoration. To accomplish this, Northstar rapidly deployed over 25 trained remediation workers and supervisors to work around the clock and complete all water extraction, debris removal, remediation and cleaning within 3 days. This allowed for the expeditious evaluation and repairs of the building operating systems. In addition, due to the region wide gasoline shortage, Northstar also provided over 10,000 gallons of gasoline to the SJU campus fuel depot so that campus vehicle including campus police could continue function.

SJU considered the post-Sandy response a great success as measured by the following:

• Continuing safety, comfort and security of the remaining students, faculty, management, clergy and staff due to the power and fuel provisioning outlined above. • Resumption of full SJU activities as soon as the region wide emergency is lifted. • The ability to institute an aggressive evaluation and repair schedule for the Manhattan Campus physical plant. • No damage to scientific research animals, extracts, cultures, media, data and analytical instrumentation resulting from the utility power outage impacting the life sciences complex. • Schedule of revenue generating events such as conferences and symposia resumed at campus facilities, including a wedding which was held at an historic building on the Oakdale long Island Campus.

projects.title: Stardust Hotel and Casino
projects.summary: Two million square feet demolished with 78% debris recycling. LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, worked with Boyd Gaming and Tishman Construction on the demolition plan. Crews abated hazardous materials and stripped the towers on an accelerated schedule ahead of the March 2007 implosion. Debris tracking supported recycling documentation for the owner.
projects.overview:
LVI collaborated with the property owner, Boyd Gaming, and general contractor, Tishman Construction of New York, over a two-year period to safely plan the abatement and implosion of the Stardust Hotel and Casino and the supporting structures that surrounded the hotel. The predemolition process included detailed development of an air quality plan for dust management, storm water pollution prevention plan, alerting the Clark County Fire Department and coordinating with the Nevada DOT for road closures and crowd control. The Stardust opened its doors in 1958 and closed them for the last time November 1, 2006 as the 45-day liquidation process began. On December 18th LVI took possession of the 27 structures on this 63-acre site. LVI self-performed all the pre-demolition hazardous material abatement on the 9-story tower, the Stardust Main Showroom and the 2-story Villa building. Site demolition began on January 2, 2007, with the lowrise outer buildings (Pavilion Building, meeting rooms, Sportsbook and Casino Building). The interior demolition of the 32-story tower hotel was performed on an accelerated schedule in order to meet the March 13th implosion date. LVI used 75-150 field technicians working on 8 floors at a time. Skid Steers were used on each floor to clear debris to the staircase well which was strategically dismantled to use as a load-out chute. Interior strip-out left concrete and steel exposed, slab to slab. Figure 1- Explosives were placed into holes bored into the columns on 5 floors of the tower. These floors were then wrapped with 2 layers of chain link fencing and special Geotex fabric to contain the debris.

It only took 10 seconds using 428 pounds of explosives to implode both the 32-story and 9-story towers. Including the outer buildings, a total of 2,000,000 square feet was demolished. LVI earned 2 LEED credits for the owner by recycling 78% of the demolition debris, such as, nonferrous metals, concrete and steel. Over 130,000 tons of concrete were crushed and recycled on site.

Load tickets were completed as each truck exited the site, and the information logged on to a spread sheet to keep track of each load. The load tickets and spread sheet were used to provide information for the owner’s LEED certification. At the time, the Stardust was the 4th largest building in the world to be imploded. LVI worked for eight weeks after the implosion finishing the cleanup of the site. Boyd Gaming is planning to re-develop this site as Echelon Place, a multifaceted destination resort with a mix of 5 unique hotels each offering its own luxury experience.

projects.title: Superdome: Phase II
projects.summary: 70,000 seats cleaned during the Superdome's recovery. NorthStar remediated affected materials and cleaned all 70,000 seats, including rust removal from seat bases. Crews used extensive scaffolding to reach contaminated materials as high as 140 feet. An air-filtration system addressed conditions throughout the dome.
projects.overview:
Gaping holes in the Superdome’s roof during and after Hurricane Katrina allowed water to damage the building’s structural materials and furnishings. Adding to the internal damages was the overcrowding of people as the sports complex became a refuge for residents seeking shelter even though all utilities had been knocked out by the storm.

NorthStar was called for the remediation of water damaged building materials and furnishings affected either by people or by the storm. NorthStar cleaned all 70,000 seats, contaminated as much by humans as by storm water, including removing the rust from the seat bases.

Extensive scaffolding was required to remove contaminated materials up to 140 feet high. NorthStar also installed an air filtering system to address the air quality in the entire dome. For the first time since Katrina the air quality in the dome was better than the air quality outside.

projects.title: UNC Wilmington: Hurricane Florence
projects.facility: University of North Carolina at Wilmington
projects.summary: Campus recovery across 130 buildings. NorthStar expanded from an initial building assignment to remediation and emergency reconstruction across 130 buildings. The team deployed 750 recovery workers, emergency-response trailers, a command center, 160,000 CFM of desiccant drying and more than 6 MW of temporary power.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Florence made landfall on the Carolina coast in September of 2018 as a Category 1 and would go on record as the wettest storm ever recorded in the Carolinas after dropping nearly 36 inches of rain. Located directly in the path of Hurricane Florence was the University of North Carolina’s Wilmington campus. During the course of the storm’s strike on the Wilmington area, significant structural damage was caused due to rising flood waters and sustained winds of 90mph. In the aftermath of the storm, University officials realized the extreme damage that had been caused and reached out to various contractors for assistance. After stretching the capabilities of various recovery firms, the decision was made to engage NorthStar for assistance.

NorthStar Recovery Services was originally assigned to one building. However, the effectiveness demonstrated by NorthStar within 24 hours of being on the job proved which firm was actually capable of completing such a large recovery project. Other recovery firms present were relieved of their commitments and NorthStar expanded to those projects as well.

Throughout the course of the project NorthStar performed remediation and emergency reconstruction on 130 buildings, including nearly 1 million square feet of affected interior space in critical residential facilities. NorthStar mobilized six 53’ and seven 32’ emergency response trailers to provide equipment and resources to the 750 recovery workers deployed across the UNCW campus. To increase efficiency and bolster communication with the client, NorthStar included one of the Command Centers in the mobilization.

In total, students residing on campus were displaced for a mere 6 weeks, a short amount of time considering the extent of the damage. 160,000CFM of desiccant drying equipment assisted in drying out affected structures as efficiently as possible, along with over 6MW of portable power generation to supplement areas where power was still out and to restore operation to buildings that would have otherwise been unusable. After only four weeks NorthStar began turning buildings over to the University and ultimately was able to salvage the semester by preventing students from losing critical class time and delaying graduation.

Nearly 200,000 man hours were worked on a 24-7 schedule, NorthStar outworked and outperformed the competition in each and every aspect of the recovery and reconstruction process. The capability, efficiency, safety, and professionalism demonstrated during the course of this project serve as a testament to why NorthStar is the nation’s leading Disaster Recovery Firm.

projects.title: UNC Wilmington: Roof Recovery
projects.facility: University of North Carolina at Wilmington
projects.summary: Roof recovery across 175 damaged rooftops. NorthStar assessed conditions with drones and thermal imaging, installed emergency protection and brought in roofing specialists. More than 90 tradespeople and thirty 80-foot articulating boom lifts supported repair work. Crews worked around the clock with the facilities team and prioritized student housing.
projects.overview:
Hurricane Florence made landfall near Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina, on September 14, 2018. Strong winds and heavy rain damaged facilities at the University of North Carolina Wilmington. Roof damage threatened further water intrusion into campus buildings.

NorthStar used drones and thermal imaging to assess conditions. The team identified 175 damaged university rooftops, on and off campus, including 60 with substantial damage. Many required emergency tarping to limit secondary damage to interiors.

NorthStar brought in roofing specialists from across the country. More than 90 specialized tradespeople and thirty 80-foot articulating boom lifts supported the repairs.

Crews worked around the clock, seven days a week, coordinating with campus facilities. Residence halls were prioritized because of the effect on students. The project account describes a six-week displacement period for resident students; this is separate from individual roof repair durations and the academic calendar.

NorthStar completed the roof repairs needed to return the affected structures to use and support the resumption of classes and campus housing.

projects.title: UNCW Cornerstone Residence Hall
projects.summary: Cornerstone restored in a three-week project. NorthStar deployed more than 60,000 CFM of desiccant drying and 1 MW of portable generation. A workforce of nearly 120 laborers, tradespeople and recovery specialists coordinated with campus facilities, contributing more than 51,000 working hours to drying and restoration.
projects.overview:
In the wake of Hurricane Florence, perhaps one of the most challenging tasks for UNC Wilmington was the relocation of many of its on-campus residents due to storm damage to residential facilities. Nearly all residence halls had incurred damage, some much worse than others. One of the most damaged dormitories was Cornerstone, which experienced significant roof damage that facilitated interior water intrusion on all three floors. Sadly, the damage was not limited to the structure alone-many students had possessions within the individual rooms including school books, computer systems, and other valuables.

NorthStar made Once engaged, NorthStar personnel and equipment were mobilized to begin the recovery process. In order to quickly and efficiently dry and repair the Cornerstone Residence Hall, over 60,000CFM of desiccant drying equipment was employed along with 1MW of portable power generation. Due to NorthStar’s quick response and employment of critical drying equipment, the extent of secondary damages was significantly reduced.

NorthStar worked hand-in-hand with campus facilities personnel to coordinate recovery operations and ensure minimal disruption to the students and faculty’s day-to-day activities. A work force of nearly 120 laborers, specialized tradesmen, and various other recovery specialists put in over 51,000 man hours to ensure that the Cornerstone was restored to pre-loss conditions quickly, efficiently, and safely. In total the project took just three weeks, a short amount of time given the extent of the damage.

Students who call the Cornerstone home were displaced for only 2 weeks and were thankful to NorthStar for saving the semester, avoiding a detrimental delay to the academic curriculum.

projects.overview:

NorthStar successfully coordinated multiple trades to work in concert to stay on schedule and within the budget. Consistent and effective project management provided vital information regarding schedule and scope issues allowing the University the opportunity to make informed decisions.

projects.title: University of Mississippi: Freeze Recovery
projects.summary: Freeze recovery completed in four weeks. NorthStar deployed desiccant drying and supporting equipment, removed damaged drywall and ceiling materials, and completed cleaning and disinfection. Reconstruction then replaced removed materials to restore the affected areas to their pre-loss condition.
projects.overview:
Adhering to the highest standards (IICRC S500), our scope of work included:

Rapid Drying and Stabilization: Immediate deployment of desiccant drying systems and other equipment to expedite the drying process.

Targeted Material Removal: Strategic removal of affected drywall, ceiling tiles, and other materials to minimize disruption and maximize efficiency.

Thorough Cleaning and Disinfection: Application of EPA-approved antimicrobial encapsulates to ensure a safe and sanitized environment.

Expert Reconstruction: Restoring all removed materials to their original state, ensuring the university's facilities were back to their pre-loss condition.

Despite the extensive damage and initial delays due to extreme weather, NorthStar's coordinated efforts and robust resources ensured a smooth and efficient recovery process. Our team's dedication and expertise turned a challenging situation into a successful recovery story.

Completed in just four weeks with zero safety incidents, this project stands as a testament to NorthStar's commitment to excellence. Our quick response and meticulous execution minimized disruption, allowing the University of Mississippi to resume normal operations swiftly.

projects.title: Historic DC Courthouse
projects.summary: Engineered demolition within a historic courthouse. As part of the Hensel Phelps team, NorthStar protected ornamental plaster, marble, moldings, doors and the grand staircase. Engineering studies informed demolition loads. Perimeter shoring and bracing allowed removal of load-bearing walls and floor slabs for a new multistory atrium.
projects.overview:
The Historic DC Courthouse in Washington's Judiciary Square required selective and structural demolition as part of a major restoration for the District of Columbia Court of Appeals. NorthStar joined the Hensel Phelps team for work in the 48,000-square-foot historic building. As environmental conditions were discovered, the scope expanded to include asbestos and lead abatement and mold remediation.

The work required protection of the grand staircase, ornamental plaster, marble flooring, crown moldings, doors and frames. Selected architectural details were removed and protected until they could be refurbished and returned after work in the area was completed.

Engineering studies evaluated the existing building before demolition to address the loads imposed by planned selective and structural work. Engineered perimeter shoring and bracing allowed removal of load-bearing walls and floor slabs on the north side to create a multistory atrium lobby.

The project period was May 2006 to November 2007. It formed part of the wider courthouse restoration and expansion, rather than the entirety of that construction program.

projects.title: W New York: Times Square
projects.summary: A one-week response across more than 40 guest rooms. NorthStar provided water extraction, moisture control, dehumidification and disinfection. A twelve-person crew worked for one week on the affected hotel areas, addressing water damage and the conditions that could lead to mold growth.
projects.overview:
NorthStar Recovery Services provided Emergency Response Services for W New York Hotel in Times Square New York when two separate pipe breaks caused water damage to over 10 of the hotel’s 56 floors. W New York - Times Square is in the heart of the theater district, with museums a few blocks north and downtown a quick subway ride away. Its location makes it a popular spot for guests so NRS had to complete the project quickly and efficiently to prevent disruption of business.

NorthStar Recovery Services provided water extraction, moisture control and dehumidification and disinfected areas to prevent the possibility of mold growth. NRS worked with a crew of twelve for one week, on over 40 rooms damaged from the pipe breaks that flooded the 21st through the 11th floor of the building.

NorthStar completed the project on schedule to the client’s satisfaction. The team was praised for their professionalism and exceptional service.

projects.summary: Phased remediation progressed at one floor per week. NorthStar first treated floors 21 through 19, then returned for additional work on floors 12 through 4 and 23 through 22. Crews removed affected drywall and wall coverings in guest rooms and corridors, coordinating with the general contractor and environmental consultant.
projects.overview:
The Westin Galleria located at 5060 W. Alabama St., Houston, TX 77056 started remodeling in early December 2016. This remodel scope (designed for Xengia Hotel Ownership) included selective demolition and new finishes on all guest floors 4-23, selective demolition and new lay out of floor 24 including the Monarch Room dining hall/ convention suite, and level 2 lobby remodel. When work began on the 21st floor Lippe Construction, the general contractor working for Xengia Hotels, discovered a mold problem after pulling the vinyl wall covering. ATC Group Services was brought in as the environmental consultant.

NorthStar started on the contaminationon the 21st floor and worked floor by floor down to the 19th floor with time for build back before Super Bowl week which was an important revenue time for the hotel.

NorthStar was brought back after a break to continue the mold remediation work on floors 12-4 and floors 23-22. The work on each floor consisted of the proper removal and disposal of mold affected sheet rock and two layers of vinyl wall covering in the bathroom and adjoining room walls in 26 rooms and two layers of vinyl wall covering and mold affected sheet rock as necessary in the hallway connecting the rooms on each floor, ice dispensing room connected to the hallway on floor 12. This work was completed at a rate of one floor per week including the necessary time for air scrubbing and clearances.

NorthStar was able to develop good working relationships with Lippe Construction, the on-site general contractor and Xengia Hotels, the owner which has already lead to other scopes of work in the Westin Galleria and Other Hotels.

projects.title: Westinghouse Electric Company
projects.summary: Contaminated equipment removed; building demolition deferred. NorthStar/LVI, a NorthStar predecessor, removed process equipment and components, segregated and reduced materials, and packaged wastes for licensed disposal or recycling. Radiation-protection support and nuclear-safety evaluations addressed recovery of special nuclear material from the process buildings.
projects.overview:
The Westinghouse nuclear fuel-manufacturing facility at Hematite, Missouri, ceased production in 2002 after nearly 47 years of operations. Its historical activities included uranium-metal and compound production, nuclear-fuel processing, research and development, scrap recovery and work involving highly enriched uranium.

The November 2003–January 2006 NorthStar/LVI engagement covered removal of contaminated equipment and components from process buildings, with an option for later demolition to slab. The buildings in scope were Building 240, Recycle and Recovery; Building 253, Uranium Powder Storage; Building 254, Pellet Plant; Building 255, Erbia Plant; Building 256-1, Pellet Drying; Building 256-2, Warehouse; and Building 260, Oxide and Oxide Loading Dock.

Crews removed equipment and components, segregated and reduced materials, and packaged radioactive and hazardous wastes for shipment and disposal. The work included debris and contaminated soil for disposal at Envirocare of Utah and materials for a licensed radiological-metals recycler in Canada. Recovery and management of accumulated hazardous chemicals were added to LVI's scope.

Radiation-protection support, equipment and monitoring supported the work under Westinghouse NRC License SNM-33. Nuclear-safety evaluations and documentation addressed recovery of special nuclear material where criticality concerns existed.

At demobilization in January 2006, the license amendment permitting building demolition to slab had not been approved. Westinghouse therefore deferred that demolition. The equipment-removal engagement ended without a lost-workday incident and earned a reported $50,000 safety bonus.

The NRC subsequently issued the Hematite license-termination notice on September 26, 2018 after later decommissioning activities. That final site-release milestone is separate from this 2003–2006 scope.

projects.overview:
This engagement associated with World Trade Center communications recovery ran from September 2001 through August 2002, with a project value of $10 million.

Crews responded within days of the September 11 attacks and participated alongside other contractors in the Lower Manhattan recovery operation. Work included debris handling, truck transport and transfers through waterfront facilities.

The team contributed personnel, equipment and logistics support to the shared recovery effort. The response brought sustained physical and emotional demands for everyone involved.

projects.summary: Debris-removal support for a shared recovery effort. Workers reached the World Trade Center site within days. Alongside other contractors, crews removed debris, loaded trucks and supported transfers through the waterfront transport system. The work formed part of the larger coordinated response in Lower Manhattan.
projects.overview:
Crews arrived at the World Trade Center site within days of the September 11, 2001 attacks to support the coordinated search and recovery operation. The work involved heavy debris, extreme heat and the responsibility of assisting the search for victims.

Alongside other contractors, workers removed debris, loaded trucks and supported transport through waterfront transfer points. The project account describes unusually large structural-steel pieces and heat conditions that made removal particularly difficult.

Debris from the wider World Trade Center recovery was taken to Fresh Kills on Staten Island for examination and processing by the responsible agencies. NorthStar's described engagement ran from September 2001 to March 2002 and contributed personnel, equipment and transport capacity to the collective operation.

The work was both a professional and personal challenge for the people involved. Whole-site recovery quantities and completion milestones belong to the wider multi-agency effort and are not presented as the output of this individual contract.

projects.title: Yale-New Haven Hospital
projects.summary: Hospital site preparation with 90% material recycling. NorthStar performed abatement for the hospital and demolition under Turner Construction. Crews used containment for asbestos removal and addressed other regulated materials and underground tanks. Interior soft demolition separated nonstructural materials before further demolition, while metals were salvaged for recycling.
projects.overview:
NorthStar has a long-standing working relationship with both Yale New Haven Hospital and its construction manager, Turner Construction. In this project scope, the abatement was directly with the hospital and the demolition was contracted with Turner. The 1940’s six-story, 60,000 square-foot building, which also included a basement and a sub-grade 10-foot wide tunnel system used for equipment maintenance, was scheduled to be demolished to make room for a new Yale Cancer Center.

The new Smilow Cancer Hospital project is the first hospital in Connecticut to register for Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Green Building rating certification. Ninety percent of the Grace Building materials were recycled for the building of the new 14-story, 497,000 square foot hospital, helping to earn LEED Gold certification.

Pre-demolition activities included building containments to remove floor tile, pipe insulation, asbestos roofing, asbestos damp proofing, as well as PCB containing ballasts, mercury containing bulbs and switches, halon, CFC’s and three underground storage tanks.

For the interior demolition, NorthStar performed what is referred to as a “soft gut” where nonstructural walls, doors, and sheet rock are removed to keep the demolition debris “clean.” At the same time, metals, some precious like copper and aluminum, and some structural steel, were salvaged and recycled.

projects.title: CCR Basin Closure — Wilmington
projects.facility: Coal ash basins and on-site landfill
projects.summary: Moving millions of cubic yards of coal ash while managing deep water, limited landfill capacity and coastal storms.
projects.overview:
A mandated closure schedule required two Wilmington coal ash basins to be emptied while environmental controls remained in place. Trans Ash, a NorthStar company, took on a scope involving approximately four million cubic yards of coal combustion residuals (CCR), on-site landfill placement, basin decommissioning and landfill closure.

The two basins demanded different removal methods: one held material as deep as 60 feet below the water table, while the other had a liner that needed to remain intact. Trans Ash combined GPS-guided mechanical excavation with hydraulic dredging and dewatering. As landfill cells became available, the team coordinated material moisture, truck movements and placement to make the most of the available disposal footprint.

Heavy rainfall and a hurricane disrupted access and damaged work areas. The team adjusted staffing and operating hours, activated an emergency response plan and developed vegetation methods suited to sandy temporary cover. The source reports a peak of 26,000 tons hauled in one day within a scope that included 1.3 million cubic yards of hydraulic dredging. A final closure date is not stated.

projects.title: CCR Basin Closure — Roxboro
projects.period: Twelve-year closure program; calendar dates not stated
projects.facility: Coal ash basins and lined landfill
projects.summary: Building disposal capacity first so a 14.5-million-cubic-yard coal ash excavation program could advance.
projects.overview:
At Roxboro, landfill construction set the pace for a much larger basin-closure program. Trans Ash, a NorthStar company, joined during design to help plan the excavation of 14.5 million cubic yards of coal combustion residuals across approximately 300 acres of basins. NorthStar's profile describes a twelve-year program with more than 81 acres of landfill construction.

Early involvement allowed excavation methods, haul routes and disposal phasing to shape the design. Groundwater required substantial earthwork across the landfill footprint, and winter construction imposed tight moisture and compaction requirements on clay and liner installation. Trans Ash operated multiple borrow areas and haul routes and imported clay to support the critical early landfill work.

The team also delivered a deep soil-mixed gravity retaining wall with specialist engineering and construction partners. The source reports completion of that wall component on schedule and under budget, alongside CCR production exceeding two million cubic yards per year. These are documented milestones within the program; overall basin-closure completion is not established.

projects.title: One Post Office Square
projects.facility: Occupied office tower and parking garage
projects.summary: Removing an office tower's façade while seven upper floors remained occupied.
projects.overview:
Floors 31 through 37 remained occupied as One Post Office Square underwent a major transformation in Boston's Financial District. NorthStar's demolition and asbestos-abatement package reached from an adjacent seven-story parking garage to the tower's interiors and exterior façade, requiring removal methods suited to an occupied high-rise.

More than 800 precast concrete panels and 1,700 windows were removed. Custom attachments supported controlled panel handling, while crews on suspended staging cut openings at occupied levels so the new curtain wall could connect to the existing steel. Interior demolition extended across multiple floors, the lobby and mechanical areas as the adjacent garage was taken down.

Multiple shifts and a workforce of up to 60 supported the removal sequence. NorthStar reports more than 15,000 tons of construction and demolition material removed. By March 2020, the team had recorded 77,260 work hours without first aid or an OSHA recordable; that figure represents the published progress snapshot.

projects.summary: Preparing a federal office building for renewal while recovering historic marble and removing regulated materials.
projects.overview:
Modernizing the Social Security Administration's Altmeyer Building required extensive removal of its existing interiors, façade and building components. Working for Hensel Phelps and GSA in Woodlawn, NorthStar brought asbestos and lead abatement, demolition and soil-remediation work into one enabling package, with historic marble identified for salvage.

The scope combined interior gut demolition with selected stairs, slabs and canopy removal. Elevators were dismantled in their entirety, including cabs, rails, motors and counterweights, and the façade was removed. Outside, crews cleared landscaping, performed rough grading and excavated contaminated soil for transport and disposal. Together, these activities prepared the existing structure and site for the broader modernization.

projects.title: Ritz-Carlton Naples — Renovation Program
projects.facility: Beachfront resort, guestroom towers, spa and public spaces
projects.summary: Recovering a guestroom schedule and sequencing demolition across a resort's expanding renovation program.
projects.overview:
The Ritz-Carlton Naples expansion needed both a new tower connection and a guestroom renovation schedule brought back on track. NorthStar's first work for PCL Construction Services began in May 2021 with selective removal of the South Tower and spa exterior. The team then took on guestroom demolition on levels 3 through 14, clearing a reported 12 rooms per day to help recover the schedule.

Across four contracts, the assignment grew to include spa, restaurant and retail interiors, the lobby and the North Tower guestrooms. Dust-control partitions separated occupied areas, while an external debris chute supported room-by-room removal. The lobby base scope finished ahead of schedule, allowing crews to accommodate additional owner-directed changes.

Hurricane Ian introduced further demolition needs at the central energy plant and Nolita Restaurant. NorthStar continued through those changing requirements within the renovation program. The property's emergency power and cooling work is covered in the separate Ritz-Carlton Naples recovery case.

projects.title: 273 Georgia Street — Blizzard Recovery
projects.summary: Addressing freeze damage and hazardous materials after a blizzard left a Buffalo residential building without heat.
projects.overview:
Days without power and heat during the December 23, 2022 Buffalo blizzard caused water and heating pipes to burst at 273 Georgia Street. The resulting repair work required selective demolition alongside controlled removal of regulated materials.

Whitney Neighborhood LLC engaged NorthStar for asbestos abatement, universal-waste collection and selective demolition. The contract ran from March 2023 through June 2024, addressing the damaged building through a defined removal scope. NorthStar reports more than 8,500 work hours without injury or regulatory violations.

projects.title: Sibley Building Adaptive Reuse
projects.facility: Historic department store converted to mixed use
projects.summary: Making room for new uses inside Rochester's historic Sibley department store.
projects.overview:
The Sibley Building's transition from department store to retail, offices and apartments required targeted changes within a substantial historic structure. At the 1.1-million-square-foot Rochester property, NorthStar supported WinnCompanies with a defined abatement and demolition contract during the wider redevelopment.

Crews removed selected asbestos-containing materials and universal waste, performed interior and structural demolition, and saw-cut chases for new services. That combination addressed existing materials while creating the openings needed for renovation. The project profile records 12,000 safe work hours at the time of writing..

projects.title: Rockland Psychiatric Hospital Site Clearance
projects.facility: Former hospital campus and tunnel network
projects.summary: Coordinating demolition, drainage and contaminated-soil removal to meet a six-month campus-clearance schedule.
projects.overview:
Six months were available to clear buildings and tunnels at the former Rockland Psychiatric Hospital campus for redevelopment. Structure Tone brought in NorthStar for a program in which demolition, contaminated-soil removal and erosion controls had to advance together across multiple work areas.

NorthStar mobilized more than 25 excavators and six portable concrete-crushing plants, supported by loaders, off-road trucks and grading equipment. Crews tracked soil-remediation areas on a grid so affected material could be removed and sent to approved off-site facilities. Catch basins, large concrete pipes, swales and a settling pond formed part of the drainage work.

Continual coordination tied building and tunnel removal to the changing drainage and soil-remediation areas. Despite unforeseen conditions, NorthStar reports completing the work within the allotted six-month period.

projects.title: Massachusetts General Hospital — Campus Demolition
projects.facility: Three buildings on an active hospital campus
projects.summary: Scheduling structural demolition within eight feet of active hospital streets and sidewalks.
projects.overview:
Two buildings at Massachusetts General Hospital stood within eight feet of active pedestrian and vehicle routes. Their removal formed part of a three-building demolition and asbestos-abatement contract awarded to NorthStar as the hospital prepared its Cambridge Street site for a new clinical-care building.

Before structural work, crews removed designated asbestos-containing flooring, pipe insulation, roofing, wall and ceiling materials, and doors and windows. High-reach equipment supported demolition of Ruth Sleeper Hall, 25 North Anderson and West End House. The proximity of Ruth Sleeper Hall and West End House to active routes led the team to schedule their structural removal across multiple weekends.

NorthStar reports more than 18,000 work hours without an OSHA recordable incident, with concrete and metal recovered for recycling. The carefully sequenced enabling work prepared the campus for its next construction stage.

projects.title: Baltimore Arena Redevelopment
projects.summary: Opening up an arena's ceiling, seating bowl and stage within a one-year renovation program.
projects.overview:
Baltimore Arena's transformation into CFG Bank Arena was built around a one-year renovation and reopening schedule. NorthStar's demolition and abatement package for Clark Construction had to prepare major portions of the 60-year-old venue for new construction, from the façade to the elevated ceiling and stage.

Crews removed selected exterior components, signage and lighting and abated asbestos-containing roof topping, soffits and façade caulk. A working scaffold platform provided access to ceiling fireproofing and the suspended plaster and metal ceiling. Structural modifications extended through the seating bowl, circulation openings, stairs, escalators and floor slabs needed for new plumbing and foundations.

At the stage, the scope included removal of the fire curtain, proscenium framing, columns, walls and slabs, with abatement of stage-wall fireproofing. These removals created the openings and cleared areas needed for the arena's new configuration.

projects.title: 270 Park Avenue Deconstruction
projects.facility: Midtown office tower above active rail infrastructure
projects.summary: Bringing a Midtown tower to grade while protecting the active rail yard below.
projects.overview:
Demolition at the former 270 Park Avenue began approximately 750 feet above Midtown Manhattan, directly over Metro-North's Madison Avenue Yard. NorthStar's contract for AECOM Tishman therefore paired high-rise deconstruction with protection of the railway below, including more than 30,000 square feet of one-inch steel plate and coordination with the city's building and fire departments.

projects.title: Hoffmann-La Roche — Buildings 115 and 115A
projects.summary: Taking down a pharmaceutical facility floor by floor, then addressing the contaminated ground beneath it.
projects.overview:
Buildings 115 and 115A at Hoffmann-La Roche's Nutley campus combined offices, research laboratories and manufacturing areas within a five-story concrete-and-steel facility. Their removal required a stable top-down demolition sequence, dust controls and remediation of localized contamination as the campus prepared for future development.

Working for Torcon, NorthStar used 120-foot and 150-foot long-reach excavators to remove upper floors in a staggered sequence. Standard excavators took over nearer ground level. Machine-mounted water systems, water cannons, trucks and hose crews kept the work wet during concrete removal.

With the superstructure down, crews broke out foundation walls and footings and loaded debris for off-site disposal. The project also included excavation and approved disposal of more than 3,000 tons of PCB-contaminated soil, extending the removal package from the buildings into the affected ground.

projects.title: Hoffmann-La Roche — Building 85
projects.summary: Controlling exposure and dust while dismantling a pharmaceutical building with complex concrete floors.
projects.overview:
Asbestos and PCB contamination complicated the removal of Building 85 and adjacent structures at Hoffmann-La Roche's Nutley campus. The concrete building's double slabs and waffle decks housed systems for pharmaceutical research and manufacturing, requiring NorthStar to connect its demolition methods closely with exposure and dust controls.

Working under a contract with Sordoni Construction, the team used 120-foot and 150-foot long-reach excavators to crush and lower sections of the building. High-volume water systems at the attachments maintained wet operations; water cannons and hose crews supplemented them to control airborne dust and contaminants.

NorthStar's project profile reports completion ahead of schedule and without incident. The documented approach combined reach, removal sequencing and continuous wet methods throughout the demolition.
